translations.idiomatic: When the emperor learned that Shen and Zezhi had slandered Lu Zhi, investigators watched them and confirmed that they had plotted with Tongxuan. The emperor was enraged. He removed Dou Can from the chief ministership and soon demoted Can to secretary at Chen, Shen to registrar at Jin, Li Zezhi to secretary at Zhao, and Tongxuan to secretary at Quan.

sentences.zh: 帝召見之，親自臨 問，責以污辱近屬。

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned him for a personal audience and interrogated him, rebuking him for staining the honor of the imperial kin.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Tongxuan for a personal audience, questioned him himself, and rebuked him for dishonoring the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 行至華州長城驛，賜死。

translations.literal: When he reached Great Wall Post on Huazhou circuit, he was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Great Wall Post in Huazhou, he was ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 尋以陸贄為中書侍郎、平章事，代竇參。

translations.literal: Soon Lu Zhi was made vice director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor in place of Dou Can.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Lu Zhi was appointed vice director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor in Dou Can's place.

sentences.zh: 通微，建中四年自壽安縣令入為金部員外，召充翰林學士。

translations.literal: Tongwei, in the fourth year of Jianzhong, entered from magistrate of Shou'an as outer court director in the Ministry of Revenue and was summoned as Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: Tongwei, in the fourth year of Jianzhong, rose from magistrate of Shou'an to outer-court director in the Ministry of Revenue and was then summoned as Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 尋改職方郎中，知制誥。

translations.literal: Shortly he was changed to director in the Ministry of Personnel and drafter of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to director in the Ministry of Personnel and drafter of edicts.

sentences.zh: 與弟通玄同職禁署，人士榮之。

translations.literal: He held the same post in the forbidden secretariat as his younger brother Tongxuan; scholars regarded this as glorious.
translations.idiomatic: He served in the same forbidden secretariat as his younger brother Tongxuan, to the envy of the scholarly world.

sentences.zh: 七年，改禮部郎中，尋轉中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was changed to director in the Ministry of Rites, then transferred to Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was made director in the Ministry of Rites and soon afterward promoted to Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 通玄死，素服待罪於國門，帝特宥之，通微竟不敢為喪服。

translations.literal: When Tongxuan died, Tongwei wore plain robes and awaited punishment at the national gate; the Emperor especially pardoned him, but Tongwei in the end did not dare wear mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When Tongxuan died, Tongwei appeared at the capital gate in plain robes to await punishment. The emperor specially pardoned him, yet Tongwei still did not dare observe mourning for his brother.

sentences.zh: 通玄詞藻婉麗，帝尤憐之。

translations.literal: Tongxuan's phrasing was graceful; the Emperor especially favored him.
translations.idiomatic: Tongxuan's diction was graceful and elegant, and the emperor favored him above all others.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，昭德王皇后崩，詔李紓為諡冊文，宰相張延賞、柳渾為廟樂章。

translations.literal: In the early Zhenyuan era Empress Zhao of virtue died; the decree ordered Li Shu to draft the posthumous title and eulogy, and the chief ministers Zhang Yanshang and Liu Hun the temple hymns.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenyuan reign Empress Zhaode died. The court ordered Li Shu to draft her posthumous title and eulogy, and the chief ministers Zhang Yanshang and Liu Hun to compose the temple hymns.

sentences.zh: 及進，皆不稱旨，並召通玄重撰。

translations.literal: When these were presented none pleased; all were summoned to have Tongxuan rewrite them.
translations.idiomatic: When the drafts were submitted none satisfied the throne, and Tongxuan alone was summoned to rewrite them.

sentences.zh: 凡中旨撰述，非通玄之筆，無不慊然，重之如此。

translations.literal: For every central drafting assignment, if it was not Tongxuan's brushwork the Emperor was never satisfied — such was the esteem in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: For every important drafting assignment from the throne, if the text was not Tongxuan's the emperor was never content — such was the regard in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 王仲舒字弘中，太原人。

translations.literal: Wang Zhongshu, style name Hongzhong, was a man of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhongshu, whose courtesy name was Hongzhong, came from Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 少孤貧，事母以孝聞。

translations.literal: Orphaned young and poor, he was known for filial devotion to his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned while young and poor, he became known for filial devotion to his mother.

sentences.zh: 嗜學工文，不就鄉舉。

translations.literal: Fond of study and skilled at letters, he would not take the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning and excelled at letters, but refused to sit for the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 凡與結交，必知名之士，與楊頊、梁肅、裴樞為忘形之契。

translations.literal: Whomever he befriended had to be a man of reputation; with Yang Xian, Liang Su, and Pei Shu he formed bonds of complete intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: He would befriend only men of established reputation. With Yang Xian, Liang Su, and Pei Shu he formed friendships without reserve.

sentences.zh: 貞元十年，策試賢良方正能直言極諫等科，仲舒登乙第，超拜右拾遺。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Zhenyuan at the examination for worthies, upright men able to speak frankly and remonstrate fully, etc., Zhongshu placed in the second tier and was promoted directly to Right Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: In 794, at the examination for worthies and upright men able to speak frankly and remonstrate boldly, Zhongshu placed in the second tier and was promoted directly to Right Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 裴延齡領度支，矯誕大言，中傷良善，仲舒上疏極論之。

translations.literal: Pei Yanling headed the Revenue Commission; with inflated falsehoods and grand talk he harmed the virtuous; Zhongshu submitted a memorial arguing fully against him.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yanling headed the Revenue Commission. With boastful falsehoods he slandered the worthy, and Zhongshu submitted a memorial denouncing him at length.

sentences.zh: 累轉尚書郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to various director posts in the Six Ministries.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession through director posts in the central ministries.

sentences.zh: 元和五年，自職方郎中知制誥。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yuanhe he rose from director in the Ministry of Personnel to Drafter of Edicts.
translations.idiomatic: In 810 he advanced from director in the Ministry of Personnel to Drafter of Edicts.

sentences.zh: 仲舒文思溫雅，制誥所出，人皆傳寫。

translations.literal: Zhongshu's literary thought was warm and elegant; whatever edicts and decrees issued from him were copied by all.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongshu wrote with a warm, elegant mind, and every edict that left his desk was copied and circulated.

sentences.zh: 京兆尹楊憑為中丞李夷簡所劾，貶臨賀尉。

translations.literal: The capital intendant Yang Ping was impeached by Senior Grand Secretary Li Yijian and was demoted to district defender of Linhe.
translations.idiomatic: The capital intendant Yang Ping was impeached by the censor-in-chief Li Yijian and demoted to district defender of Linhe.

sentences.zh: 仲舒與憑善，宣言於朝，言夷簡掎摭憑罪，仲舒坐貶硤州刺史。

translations.literal: Zhongshu was friendly with Ping and proclaimed at court that Yijian had framed Ping's crimes; Zhongshu was punished by demotion to prefect of Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongshu was on friendly terms with Ping and declared openly at court that Yijian had manufactured charges against him. For this Zhongshu was demoted to prefect of Xia.

sentences.zh: 遷蘇州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred to Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，復召為中書舍人。

translations.literal: When Muzong took the throne, Zhongshu was again summoned as Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Muzong ascended the throne, Zhongshu was recalled and appointed Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 其年出為洪州刺史、御史中丞、江南西道觀察使。

translations.literal: That same year he went out as prefect of Hong, as chief of the imperial censors, and as observation commissioner of Jiangnan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he was sent out as prefect of Hong, imperial censor-in-chief, and observation commissioner of Jiangnan West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 江西前例榷酒私釀法深，仲舒至鎮，奏罷之。

translations.literal: Jiangxi had by precedent heavy laws against the wine monopoly and private brewing; when Zhongshu reached his post he memorialized to abolish them.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi had long enforced harsh laws against private brewing under the wine monopoly. When Zhongshu took up his post he memorialized to repeal them.

sentences.zh: 又出官錢二萬貫，代貧戶輸稅。

translations.literal: He also disbursed twenty thousand strings of official cash to pay taxes on behalf of poor households.
translations.idiomatic: He also drew twenty thousand strings from official funds to pay taxes for impoverished households.

sentences.zh: 長慶三年冬，卒于鎮。

translations.literal: In the winter of the third year of Changqing he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of 823 he died at his post.

sentences.zh: 崔咸。

translations.literal: Cui Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xian.

sentences.zh: 字重易。

translations.literal: Style name Chongyi.
translations.idiomatic: His courtesy name was Chongyi.

sentences.zh: 博陵人、祖安石。

translations.literal: A man of Boling; his grandfather was Anshi.
translations.idiomatic: He was from Boling; his grandfather was Anshi.

sentences.zh: 父鋭，位終給事中。

translations.literal: His father Rui ended his career as a Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: His father Rui ended his career as a supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 咸元和二年進士擢第，又登博學宏詞科。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanhe, Xian passed the jinshi examination and also passed the examination in erudite learning and grand literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: In 807 Xian passed the jinshi examination and also passed the examination in erudite learning and grand literary composition.

sentences.zh: 鄭餘慶、李夷簡辟為賔佐，待如師友。

translations.literal: Zheng Yuqing and Li Yijian recruited him as an aide and treated him like a teacher or friend.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yuqing and Li Yijian recruited him as an aide and treated him like a teacher or friend.

sentences.zh: 及登朝，歴踐臺閣，獨行守正，時望甚重。

translations.literal: When he entered court service, he successively held posts in the central offices, upright and independent in conduct, and his reputation at the time was very weighty.
translations.idiomatic: Once he entered court service, he held successive posts in the central offices, upright and independent in conduct, and enjoyed great standing at the time.

sentences.zh: 敬宗欲幸東都，人心不安，裴度以勲舊自興元隨表入覲，既至，李逢吉不欲度復入中書，京兆尹劉栖楚，逢吉黨也，栖楚等十餘人駕肩排度，而朝士持兩端者日擁度門，一日，度留客命酒，栖楚矯求度之歡曲，躬附裴耳而語，咸嫉其矯，舉爵罰度曰：丞相不當許所由官呫囁耳語！

translations.literal: When Emperor Jingzong wished to visit the Eastern Capital, hearts were unsettled. Pei Du, a meritorious elder, came from Xingyuan with a memorial to attend audience. Once he arrived, Li Fengji did not want Du to reenter the Secretariat. Liu Qichu, the metropolitan prefect of Jingzhao and a member of Fengji's faction, together with more than ten others, shouldered one another to crowd Du aside. Meanwhile court officials who hedged their bets daily thronged Du's gate. One day Du kept guests and ordered wine. Qichu affectedly sought a favorite tune of Du's, leaned close to Pei's ear, and spoke to him. Xian resented the affectation, raised his cup, and penalized Du, saying: "The chief minister ought not permit a petty official to whisper in his ear!"
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jingzong wished to visit the Eastern Capital, public unease spread. Pei Du, a meritorious elder, came from Xingyuan with a memorial to attend audience. Once he arrived, Li Fengji did not want Du to reenter the Secretariat. Liu Qichu, the metropolitan prefect of Jingzhao and a member of Fengji's faction, together with more than ten others, shouldered one another to crowd Du aside. Meanwhile court officials who hedged their bets daily thronged Du's gate. One day Du kept guests and ordered wine. Qichu affectedly sought a favorite tune of Du's, leaned close to Pei's ear, and spoke to him. Xian resented the affectation, raised his cup, and penalized Du, saying, "The chief minister ought not permit a petty official to whisper in his ear!"

sentences.zh: 度笑而飲之，栖楚不自安趨出，坐客皆壮之。

translations.literal: Du smiled and drank; Qichu, ill at ease, hurried out, and the seated guests all admired Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Du smiled and drank; Qichu, ill at ease, hurried out, and the seated guests all admired Xian.

sentences.zh: 累遷陜州大都督府長史，陜虢觀察等使，自旦至暮，與賔僚痛飲，恒醉不醒，簿領堆積，夜分省覽，剖判決斷，無毫釐之差，胥吏以為神人。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to chief administrator of the Shaan prefecture metropolitan command, and commissioner of the Shaan-Guo observation circuit. From dawn to dusk he drank heavily with his staff, constantly drunk and never sober. Official documents piled up; at midnight he reviewed them, adjudicated and decided cases, with not the slightest error, and the clerks regarded him as a divine man.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to chief administrator of the Shaan prefecture metropolitan command and commissioner of the Shaan-Guo observation circuit. From dawn to dusk he drank heavily with his staff, constantly drunk and never sober. Official documents piled up; at midnight he reviewed them, adjudicated and decided cases without the slightest error, and the clerks regarded him as a divine man.

sentences.zh: 入為右散騎常侍、秘書監，太和八年十月卒初，鋭佐李抱真為澤潞從事，有道人自稱盧老，曽事隋朝雲際寺李先生，預知過往未來之事，屬河朔禁遊客，鋭館之於家，一旦辭去且曰：我死當與君為子。

translations.literal: He entered court as Right Regular Mounted Attendant and Director of the Secretariat. In the tenth month of the eighth year of Taihe he died. Previously, Rui had served Li Baozhen as an aide in Ze-Lu. A Daoist who called himself Old Lu had once served Master Li at Yunji Temple in the Sui dynasty and could foreknow past and future events. Because the Hebei region forbade travelers, Rui lodged him at home. One day he took leave and said: "When I die I shall become your son."
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as Right Regular Mounted Attendant and Director of the Secretariat. In the tenth month of 834 he died. Previously, Rui had served Li Baozhen as an aide in Ze-Lu. A Daoist who called himself Old Lu had once served Master Li at Yunji Temple in the Sui dynasty and could foreknow past and future events. Because the Hebei region forbade travelers, Rui lodged him at home. One day he took leave and said, "When I die I shall become your son."

sentences.zh: 因指口下黒子，願以為志。

translations.literal: He pointed to a black mole below his mouth and asked that it be taken as a mark.
translations.idiomatic: He pointed to a black mole below his mouth and asked that it be taken as a mark.

sentences.zh: 咸之生也，果有黒子，其形神即盧老也，父即以盧老字之。

translations.literal: When Xian was born, he indeed had a black mole; his form and spirit were exactly those of Old Lu, and his father therefore gave him the style name Old Lu.
translations.idiomatic: When Xian was born, he indeed had a black mole; his form and spirit were exactly those of Old Lu, and his father therefore gave him the style name Old Lu.

sentences.zh: 既冠，棲心髙尚，志於林壑，往往獨遊南山，經時方還。

translations.literal: Once capped, he set his heart on lofty pursuits and aspired to forests and ravines, often wandering alone in the Southern Mountains and returning only after long intervals.
translations.idiomatic: Once capped, he set his heart on lofty pursuits and aspired to forests and ravines, often wandering alone in the Southern Mountains and returning only after long intervals.

sentences.zh: 尤長於歌詩，或風景晴明，花朝月夕，朗吟意愜，必悽愴霑襟，㫖趣高奇，名流嗟挹，有文集二十卷。

translations.literal: He was especially skilled in songs and poetry. When the scenery was clear and bright, on flower mornings and moonlit evenings, if he chanted aloud with contentment, he would inevitably be moved to sorrow and wet his collar. His intent was lofty and singular, and eminent men sighed in admiration. He had a collected writings in twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially skilled in songs and poetry. When the scenery was clear and bright, on flower mornings and moonlit evenings, if he chanted aloud with contentment, he would inevitably be moved to sorrow and wet his collar. His intent was lofty and singular, and eminent men sighed in admiration. He left a collected writings in twenty juan.

sentences.zh: 唐次，并州晉陽人也，國初功臣禮部尚書儉之後。

translations.literal: Tang Ci was a man of Jinyang in Bing prefecture, a descendant of Jian, Minister of Rites and an early founding merit-holder.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Ci was a man of Jinyang in Bing prefecture, a descendant of Jian, Minister of Rites and an early founding merit-holder.

sentences.zh: 建中初進士擢第，累辟使府。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianzhong era he passed the jinshi examination and was repeatedly recruited to commissioner staffs.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jianzhong era he passed the jinshi examination and was repeatedly recruited to commissioner staffs.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，歷侍御史，竇參深重之，轉禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhenyuan era he served as attendant censor. Dou Can deeply valued him and transferred him to Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhenyuan era he served as attendant censor. Dou Can deeply valued him and transferred him to Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 八年，參貶官，次坐出為開州刺史。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, when Can was demoted, Ci was implicated and sent out as prefect of Kai prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In 792, when Can was demoted, Ci was implicated and sent out as prefect of Kai prefecture.

sentences.zh: 在巴峽間十餘年，不獲進用。

translations.literal: For more than ten years among the Ba gorges he did not obtain further advancement.
translations.idiomatic: For more than ten years among the Ba gorges he did not obtain further advancement.

sentences.zh: 西川節度使韋臯抗表請為副使，德宗密諭臯令罷之。

translations.literal: Wei Gao, military governor of Xichuan, submitted a forceful memorial requesting him as deputy commissioner, but Dezong secretly instructed Gao to withdraw the request.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Gao, military governor of Xichuan, submitted a forceful memorial requesting him as deputy commissioner, but Dezong secretly instructed Gao to withdraw the request.

sentences.zh: 次久滯蠻荒，孤心抑鬱，怨謗所積，孰與申明，乃採自古忠臣賢士，遭罹讒謗放逐，遂至殺身，而君猶不悟，其書三篇，謂之辨謗略，上之。

translations.literal: Ci long lingered in the barbarian wilds, solitary and depressed, with resentments and slanders accumulating with no one to clarify them. He therefore gathered loyal ministers and worthy men of old who had suffered slander, exile, and banishment, even to the point of losing their lives while their rulers still failed to understand, and composed three treatises called A Brief Account for Refuting Slander, which he submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Ci long lingered in the barbarian wilds, solitary and depressed, with resentments and slanders accumulating and no one to clarify them. He therefore gathered loyal ministers and worthy men of old who had suffered slander, exile, and banishment, even to the point of losing their lives while their rulers still failed to understand, and composed three treatises called A Brief Account for Refuting Slander, which he submitted.

sentences.zh: 德宗省之，猶怒，謂左右曰：「唐次乃方吾為古之昏主，何自諭如此！」

translations.literal: Dezong reviewed them and was still angry, saying to those around him: "Tang Ci is comparing me to an ancient benighted ruler—why would he admonish me in this way!"
translations.idiomatic: Dezong reviewed them and was still angry, saying to those around him, "Tang Ci is comparing me to an ancient benighted ruler—why would he admonish me in this way!"

sentences.zh: 改夔州刺史。

translations.literal: He was reassigned as prefect of Kui prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as prefect of Kui prefecture.

sentences.zh: 憲宗即位，與李吉甫同自峽內召還，授次禮部郎中。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzong took the throne, he and Li Jifu were summoned back together from within the gorges and Ci was appointed Director of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzong took the throne, he and Li Jifu were summoned back together from within the gorges and Ci was appointed Director of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 尋以本官知制誥，正拜中書舍人，卒。

translations.literal: Soon, while retaining his original office, he was made Drafting Secretary; he was then formally appointed Secretariat Drafter and died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, while retaining his original office, he was made drafting secretary; he was then formally appointed Secretariat drafter and died.

sentences.zh: 章武皇帝明哲嫉惡，尤惡人朋比傾陷，嘗閱書禁中，得次所上書三篇，覽而善之，謂學士沈傳師曰：「唐次所集辨謗之書，實君人者時宜觀覽。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhangwu was wise, discerning, and hated evil, especially detesting factional collusion and framed accusations. Once in the inner palace he came upon the three treatises Ci had submitted, read them with approval, and said to Academician Shen Chuanshi: "The book Tang Ci compiled on refuting slander is indeed something a ruler should read at the proper time.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhangwu was wise, discerning, and hated evil, especially detesting factional collusion and framed accusations. Once in the inner palace he came upon the three treatises Ci had submitted, read them with approval, and said to Academician Shen Chuanshi, "The book Tang Ci compiled on refuting slander is indeed something a ruler should read at the proper time.

sentences.zh: 朕思古書中多有此事，次編錄未盡。

translations.literal: I think ancient books contain many such cases, and Ci's compilation is not exhaustive.
translations.idiomatic: I think ancient books contain many such cases, and Ci's compilation is not exhaustive.

sentences.zh: 卿家傳史學，可與學士類例廣之。」

translations.literal: Your family transmits the study of history; you may, with the academicians, broaden it by category and example."
translations.idiomatic: Your family transmits the study of history; you may, with the academicians, broaden it by category and example."

sentences.zh: 傳師奉詔與令狐楚、杜元穎等分功脩續，廣為十卷，號元和辨謗略，其序曰：臣聞乾坤定而上下分矣，至於播四時之候，遂萬物之宜，在驗乎妖、祥之二氣，祥氣降則為豐為茂，妖氣降則為沴為災。

translations.literal: Chuanshi received the edict and, with Linghu Chu, Du Yuanying, and others, divided the labor of revision and continuation, expanded it to ten juan, and titled it the Yuanhe Brief Account for Refuting Slander. Its preface says: I have heard that once Heaven and Earth were fixed, high and low were divided; as for spreading the seasons of the four times and completing what is fitting for the myriad things, this lies in testing the two qi of portent and blessing—when blessing qi descends there is abundance and luxuriance, when portent qi descends there is pestilence and disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanshi received the edict and, with Linghu Chu, Du Yuanying, and others, divided the labor of revision and continuation, expanded it to ten juan, and titled it the Yuanhe Brief Account for Refuting Slander. Its preface says: I have heard that once Heaven and Earth were fixed, high and low were divided; as for spreading the seasons of the four times and completing what is fitting for the myriad things, this lies in testing the two qi of portent and blessing—when blessing qi descends there is abundance and luxuriance, when portent qi descends there is pestilence and disaster.

sentences.zh: 君臣立而卑高隔矣，至於處神明之奧，詢獻納之辭，在審乎邪、正之二說，正言勝則為忠為讜，邪言勝則為讒為諛。

translations.literal: Once ruler and minister were established, high and low were separated; as for dwelling in the inner mystery of the divine and examining words of submission and remonstrance, this lies in scrutinizing the two doctrines of perverse and upright—when upright words prevail there is loyalty and forthright counsel, when perverse words prevail there is slander and flattery.
translations.idiomatic: Once ruler and minister were established, high and low were separated; as for dwelling in the inner mystery of the divine and examining words of submission and remonstrance, this lies in scrutinizing the two doctrines of perverse and upright—when upright words prevail there is loyalty and forthright counsel, when perverse words prevail there is slander and flattery.

sentences.zh: 故詩云：「萋兮斐兮，成是貝錦。」

translations.literal: Therefore the Odes say: "Luxuriant, patterned—thus is the shell brocade made."
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the Odes say, "Luxuriant, patterned—thus is the shell brocade made."

sentences.zh: 刺其組織之甚巧也。

translations.literal: This satirizes how very artfully such things are woven together.
translations.idiomatic: This satirizes how very artfully such things are woven together.

sentences.zh: 語曰：「邪徑敗良田，讒口亂善人。」

translations.literal: A saying goes: "A crooked path ruins good fields; slanderous mouths overturn good men."
translations.idiomatic: A saying goes, "A crooked path ruins good fields; slanderous mouths overturn good men."

sentences.zh: 惡其莠言之蠹政也。

translations.literal: This condemns how weedy words are pests to government.
translations.idiomatic: This condemns how weedy words are pests to government.

sentences.zh: 蓋謂似信而詐，似忠而非，便便可以動心，捷捷可以亂德，豈止鶗鳺彫卉，薏苡惑珠者哉！

translations.literal: It means that what seems trustworthy is deceitful, what seems loyal is not; what is convenient can move the heart, what is glib can disorder virtue—this is not limited to the cuckoo staining flowers or coix seed confusing pearls!
translations.idiomatic: It means that what seems trustworthy is deceitful, what seems loyal is not; what is convenient can move the heart, what is glib can disorder virtue—this is not limited to the cuckoo staining flowers or coix seed confusing pearls!

sentences.zh: 況立國家，自中徂外，道偏則刑罰不中，讒勝則忠孝靡彰。

translations.literal: Moreover, in establishing a state, from the center to the outer reaches, if the Way is skewed punishments will not hit the mark; if slander prevails loyalty and filial piety will not be displayed.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in establishing a state, from the center to the outer reaches, if the Way is skewed punishments will not hit the mark; if slander prevails loyalty and filial piety will not be displayed.

sentences.zh: 逖覽前聞，緬想近古，招賢容鯁，遠佞嫉邪，慮之則深，防之未至。

translations.literal: Looking far back at former reports and thinking closely on recent antiquity, they recruited the worthy and tolerated blunt counsel, kept the sycophantic at a distance and hated the perverse, yet though they pondered deeply, they did not reach the point of prevention.
translations.idiomatic: Looking far back at former reports and thinking closely on recent antiquity, they recruited the worthy and tolerated blunt counsel, kept the sycophantic at a distance and hated the perverse, yet though they pondered deeply, they did not reach the point of prevention.

sentences.zh: 伏惟睿聖文武皇帝陛下，垂衣御宇，化洽文明，謨猷博訪於縉紳，旌賁屢臻於巖穴。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Your Sagely, Wise, and Martial Majesty, draped in rule over the realm, with transforming influence reaching refined civilization, broadly seeks plans among the gentry and repeatedly sends honors to recluses in mountain caves.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly consider that Your Sagely, Wise, and Martial Majesty, draped in rule over the realm, with transforming influence reaching refined civilization, broadly seeks plans among the gentry and repeatedly sends honors to recluses in mountain caves.

sentences.zh: 尚復廣四目，周四聦，制理皆在於未萌，作範將垂於不朽。

translations.literal: You further broaden the four eyes and extend the four ears, so that regulation and order are all addressed before they sprout, and the model you establish will be handed down imperishably.
translations.idiomatic: You further broaden the four eyes and extend the four ears, so that regulation and order are all addressed before they sprout, and the model you establish will be handed down imperishably.

sentences.zh: 乃詔掌文之臣令狐楚等，上自周、漢，下洎隋朝，求史籍之忠賢，罹讒謗之事跡，敘瑕釁之本末，紀謠諑之淺深，編次指明，勒成十卷。

translations.literal: Thereupon you ordered the literary officials Linghu Chu and others, from Zhou and Han above down through the Sui dynasty, to seek in historical records loyal and worthy men and the traces of those who suffered slander, narrate the beginning and end of faults and offenses, record the depth and shallowness of rumor and slander, arrange them in order with clarity, and compile them into ten juan.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon you ordered the literary officials Linghu Chu and others, from Zhou and Han above down through the Sui dynasty, to seek in historical records loyal and worthy men and the traces of those who suffered slander, narrate the beginning and end of faults and offenses, record the depth and shallowness of rumor and slander, arrange them in order with clarity, and compile them into ten juan.

sentences.zh: 昔虞舜有堲讒之命，我皇脩辨謗之書，千古一心，同垂至理。

translations.literal: Formerly Yu Shun had the command to eliminate slander; our emperor has revised the book for refuting slander—through a thousand ages one mind, together handing down supreme principle.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Yu Shun had the command to eliminate slander; our emperor has revised the book for refuting slander—through a thousand ages one mind, together handing down supreme principle.

sentences.zh: 將俟法宮退日昃之政，別殿備乙夜之觀，則聖慮先辨，謗何由興，上天不言，而民自信矣。

translations.literal: When the imperial palace withdraws from governance at the slanting of the sun and a separate hall is prepared for reading deep into the second watch, then sagely consideration will first discern slander—how can slander arise? Heaven does not speak, yet the people will trust of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial palace withdraws from governance at the slanting of the sun and a separate hall is prepared for reading deep into the second watch, then sagely consideration will first discern slander—how can slander arise? Heaven does not speak, yet the people will trust of themselves.

sentences.zh: 憲宗優詔荅之。

translations.literal: Xianzong replied with a gracious edict.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong replied with a gracious edict.

sentences.zh: 次子扶、持。

translations.literal: His second sons were Fu and Chi.
translations.idiomatic: His second sons were Fu and Chi.

sentences.zh: 扶，字雲翔。

translations.literal: Fu, style name Yunxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Fu, whose courtesy name was Yunxiang.

sentences.zh: 元和五年進士登第進士登第，累佐使府。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yuanhe he passed the jinshi examination and repeatedly served on commissioner staffs.
translations.idiomatic: In 810 he passed the jinshi examination and repeatedly served on commissioner staffs.

sentences.zh: 入朝為監察御史，出為刺史。

translations.literal: He entered court as a supervisory censor and went out as a prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as a supervisory censor and went out as a prefect.

sentences.zh: 大和初，入朝為屯田郎中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Dahe era he entered court as Director of the Directorate of Waterways and Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Dahe era he entered court as Director of the Directorate of Waterways and Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 五年，充山南道宣撫使，至鄧州，奏：「內鄉縣行市、黃澗兩場倉督鄧琬等，先主掌湖南、江西運到糙米，至淅川縣於荒野中囤貯，除支用外，六千九百四十五石，裛爛成灰塵。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was made pacification commissioner of the Shannan circuit. Reaching Deng prefecture, he memorialized: "The warehouse supervisors Deng Wan and others of the Xingshi and Huangjian markets in Neixiang county previously managed husked rice transported from Hunan and Jiangxi, stored in the wilds at Xichuan county; apart from what was disbursed, six thousand nine hundred forty-five shi rotted into dust.
translations.idiomatic: In 831 he was made pacification commissioner of the Shannan circuit. Reaching Deng prefecture, he memorialized, "The warehouse supervisors Deng Wan and others of the Xingshi and Huangjian markets in Neixiang county previously managed husked rice transported from Hunan and Jiangxi, stored in the wilds at Xichuan county; apart from what was disbursed, six thousand nine hundred forty-five shi rotted into dust.

sentences.zh: 度支牒徵元掌所由，自貞元二十年，鄧琬父子兄弟至玄孫，相承禁繫二十八年，前後禁死九人。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue issued a warrant to pursue the original responsible officials. From the twentieth year of Zhenyuan, Deng Wan's father, sons, brothers, down to great-great-grandsons, were successively imprisoned for twenty-eight years; nine persons died in confinement.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue issued a warrant to pursue the original responsible officials. From 804, Deng Wan's father, sons, brothers, down to great-great-grandsons, were successively imprisoned for twenty-eight years; nine persons died in confinement.

sentences.zh: 今琬孫及玄孫見在枷禁者。」

translations.literal: Wan's grandson and great-great-grandson are now still in cangue and imprisonment."
translations.idiomatic: Wan's grandson and great-great-grandson are now still in cangue and imprisonment."

sentences.zh: 勑曰：「如聞鹽鐵、度支兩使，此類極多。

translations.literal: An edict said: "As I hear, the salt-iron and revenue commissioners have extremely many cases of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "As I hear, the salt-iron and revenue commissioners have extremely many cases of this kind.

sentences.zh: 其鄧琬等四人，資產全已賣納，禁繫三代，瘐死獄中，實傷和氣。

translations.literal: As for Deng Wan and the other four men, their assets have all been sold and paid in; three generations were imprisoned and died wasted in prison—this truly harms harmonious qi.
translations.idiomatic: As for Deng Wan and the other four men, their assets have all been sold and paid in; three generations were imprisoned and died wasted in prison—this truly harms harmonious qi.

sentences.zh: 鄧琬等並疏放。

translations.literal: Deng Wan and the others are all to be released.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Wan and the others are all to be released.

sentences.zh: 天下州府監院如有此類，不得禁經三年已上。

translations.literal: In prefectures and circuits throughout the realm, if prison wards have cases of this kind, imprisonment may not extend three years or more.
translations.idiomatic: In prefectures and circuits throughout the realm, if prison wards have cases of this kind, imprisonment may not extend three years or more.

sentences.zh: 速便疏理以聞。」

translations.literal: Quickly review and report."
translations.idiomatic: Quickly review and report."

sentences.zh: 物議嘉扶有宣撫之才。

translations.literal: Public opinion praised Fu for having talent as a pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion praised Fu for having talent as a pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 俄轉司勳郎中。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Director of the Directorate of Merit.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to Director of the Directorate of Merit.

sentences.zh: 八年，充弘文館學士，判院事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was made academician of the Hongwen Institute and handled institute affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 834 he was made academician of the Hongwen Institute and handled institute affairs.

sentences.zh: 九年，轉職方郎中，權知中書舍人事。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was transferred to Director of the Directorate of Military Appointments and acted as Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: In 835 he was transferred to Director of the Directorate of Military Appointments and acted as Secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 開成初，正拜舍人，踰月，授福州刺史、御史中丞、福建團練觀察使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaicheng he was formally appointed drafter; after a month he was made prefect of Fuzhou, censor-in-chief, and military training and observation commissioner of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Kaicheng he was formally appointed drafter; after a month he was made prefect of Fuzhou, censor-in-chief, and military training and observation commissioner of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 四年十一月，卒于鎮。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the fourth year he died in his post.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of 839 he died in his post.

sentences.zh: 扶佐幕立事，登朝有名，及廉問甌、閩，政事不治。

translations.literal: Fu had established himself assisting in staffs and had a name upon entering court, but when he conducted inspection tours in Ou and Min his governance was not well ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Fu had established himself assisting in staffs and had a name upon entering court, but when he conducted inspection tours in Ou and Min his governance was not well ordered.

sentences.zh: 身歿之後，僕妾爭財，詣闕論訴，法司按劾，其家財十萬貫，歸於二妾。

translations.literal: After his death, servants and concubines fought over property, went to the palace gate to plead, and the legal offices investigated; his household wealth of one hundred thousand strings went to two concubines.
translations.idiomatic: After his death, servants and concubines fought over property, went to the palace gate to plead, and the legal offices investigated; his household wealth of one hundred thousand strings went to two concubines.

sentences.zh: 又嘗枉殺部人，為其家所訴。

translations.literal: He had also once wrongly killed a subordinate, and was sued by that man's family.
translations.idiomatic: He had also once wrongly killed a subordinate, and was sued by that man's family.

sentences.zh: 行己前後不類，時論非之。

translations.literal: His conduct before and after was inconsistent, and contemporary opinion criticized him.
translations.idiomatic: His conduct before and after was inconsistent, and contemporary opinion criticized him.

sentences.zh: 持，字徳守。

translations.literal: Chi, style name Deshou.
translations.idiomatic: Chi, whose courtesy name was Deshou.

sentences.zh: 元和十五年擢進士第，累辟諸侯府。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Yuanhe he passed the jinshi examination and was repeatedly recruited to feudal staffs.
translations.idiomatic: In 820 he passed the jinshi examination and was repeatedly recruited to feudal staffs.

sentences.zh: 入朝為侍御史、尚書郎。

translations.literal: He entered court as attendant censor and director in the ministries.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as attendant censor and director in the ministries.

sentences.zh: 大中末，自工部郎中出為容州刺史、御史中丞、容管經略招討使。

translations.literal: At the end of the Dazhong era he went out from Vice Director of the Ministry of Works as prefect of Rong, censor-in-chief, and military commissioner of Rongguan for pacification and suppression.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Dazhong era he went out from Vice Director of the Ministry of Works as prefect of Rong, censor-in-chief, and military commissioner of Rongguan for pacification and suppression.

sentences.zh: 入為給事中。

translations.literal: He entered court as Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 大中末，檢校左散騎常侍、靈州大都督府長史、朔方節度、靈武六城轉運等使。

translations.literal: At the end of Dazhong he was made acting Left Regular Mounted Attendant, chief administrator of the Ling metropolitan command, military governor of Shuofang, and commissioner for transport of the six Lingwu cities, among other posts.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Dazhong he was made acting Left Regular Mounted Attendant, chief administrator of the Ling metropolitan command, military governor of Shuofang, and commissioner for transport of the six Lingwu cities, among other posts.

sentences.zh: 進位檢校戶部尚書、潞州大都督府長史、昭義節度、澤潞邢洺磁觀察處置等使，卒。

translations.literal: He advanced to acting Minister of Revenue, chief administrator of the Lu metropolitan command, military governor of Zhaoyi, and commissioner for observation and disposition of Ze, Lu, Xing, Ming, and Ci, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to acting Minister of Revenue, chief administrator of the Lu metropolitan command, military governor of Zhaoyi, and commissioner for observation and disposition of Ze, Lu, Xing, Ming, and Ci, and died.

sentences.zh: 子彦謙，字茂業。

translations.literal: His son Yanqian, style name Maoye.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yanqian, whose courtesy name was Maoye.

sentences.zh: 咸通末應進士，才高負氣，無所屈降，十餘年不第。

translations.literal: At the end of Xiantong he sat for the jinshi examination. Talented and proud, he would bow to no one; for more than ten years he did not pass.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Xiantong he sat for the jinshi examination. Talented and proud, he would bow to no one; for more than ten years he did not pass.

sentences.zh: 乾符末，河南盜起，兩都覆沒，以其家避地漢南。

translations.literal: At the end of Qianfu bandits rose in Henan, both capitals fell, and he moved his family to seek refuge in southern Han.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Qianfu bandits rose in Henan, both capitals fell, and he moved his family to seek refuge in southern Han.

sentences.zh: 中和中，王重榮鎮河中，辟為從事。

translations.literal: In the Zhonghe era Wang Chongrong governed Hezhong and recruited him as an aide.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhonghe era Wang Chongrong governed Hezhong and recruited him as an aide.

sentences.zh: 累奏至河中節度副使，歷晉、絳二州刺史。

translations.literal: Through repeated memorials he rose to deputy military governor of Hezhong and served as prefect of Jin and Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: Through repeated memorials he rose to deputy military governor of Hezhong and served as prefect of Jin and Jiang.

sentences.zh: 彥謙博學多藝，文詞壯麗，至於書畫音樂博飲之技，無不出於輩流。

translations.literal: Yanqian was broadly learned and multitalented; his literary language was vigorous and splendid. In painting, calligraphy, music, and skill at deep drinking, none among his peers did not excel.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqian was broadly learned and multitalented; his literary language was vigorous and splendid. In painting, calligraphy, music, and skill at deep drinking, none among his peers did not excel.

sentences.zh: 尤能七言詩，少時師溫庭筠，故文格類之。

translations.literal: He was especially skilled in heptasyllabic poetry; in youth he studied under Wen Tingyun, so his literary style resembled Wen's.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially skilled in heptasyllabic poetry; in youth he studied under Wen Tingyun, so his literary style resembled Wen's.

sentences.zh: 光啟末，王重榮為部下所害，朝議責參佐，彥謙與書記李巨川俱貶漢中掾曹。

translations.literal: At the end of Guangqi Wang Chongrong was killed by his subordinates. Court opinion blamed the aides; Yanqian and secretary Li Juchuan were both demoted to clerks in Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Guangqi Wang Chongrong was killed by his subordinates. Court opinion blamed the aides; Yanqian and secretary Li Juchuan were both demoted to clerks in Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 時楊守亮鎮興元，素聞其名，彥謙以本府參承，守亮見之，喜握手曰：「聞尚書名久矣，邂逅於茲。」

translations.literal: At the time Yang Shouliang governed Xingyuan and had long heard his name. Yanqian came as a staff member of that prefecture; Shouliang saw him, rejoiced, grasped his hand, and said: "I have long heard of the Minister's name; what a meeting here!"
translations.idiomatic: At the time Yang Shouliang governed Xingyuan and had long heard his name. Yanqian came as a staff member of that prefecture; Shouliang saw him, rejoiced, grasped his hand, and said, "I have long heard of the Minister's name; what a meeting here!"

sentences.zh: 翌日，署為判官。

translations.literal: The next day he was appointed judge.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he was appointed judge.

sentences.zh: 累官至副使，閬、壁二郡刺史。

translations.literal: Through repeated promotions he reached deputy commissioner and served as prefect of Lang and Bi.
translations.idiomatic: Through repeated promotions he reached deputy commissioner and served as prefect of Lang and Bi.

sentences.zh: 卒於漢中。

translations.literal: He died in Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 有詩數百篇，禮部侍郎薛廷珪為之序，號鹿門先生集，行於時。

translations.literal: He had several hundred poems; Vice Minister of Rites Xue Tinggui wrote a preface for them, titled Collected Works of Master Lumen, and they circulated at the time.
translations.idiomatic: He had several hundred poems; Vice Minister of Rites Xue Tinggui wrote a preface for them, titled Collected Works of Master Lumen, and they circulated at the time.

sentences.zh: 子渙，位亦至郡守。

translations.literal: His son Huan also reached prefect.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huan also reached prefect.

sentences.zh: 次弟歡、款、欣。

translations.literal: Ci's younger brothers were Huan, Kuan, and Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Ci's younger brothers were Huan, Kuan, and Xin.

sentences.zh: 款貞元六年登進士第，累辟使府，登朝為御史，出為郡守，卒。

translations.literal: Kuan passed the jinshi examination in the sixth year of Zhenyuan, was repeatedly recruited to commissioner staffs, entered court as censor, went out as prefect, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan passed the jinshi examination in 790, was repeatedly recruited to commissioner staffs, entered court as censor, went out as prefect, and died.

sentences.zh: 子枝。

translations.literal: His son Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhi.

sentences.zh: 枝字己有，會昌末，累遷刑部員外，轉郎中，累歷刺史，卒。

translations.literal: Zhi, style name Jiyou. At the end of Huichang he was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice, then director, successively served as prefect, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi, whose courtesy name was Jiyou. At the end of Huichang he was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice, then director, successively served as prefect, and died.

sentences.zh: 劉蕡，字去華，昌平人。

translations.literal: Liu Fen, style name Quhua, was a man of Changping.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fen, whose courtesy name was Quhua, was a man of Changping.

sentences.zh: 父勉。

translations.literal: His father was Mian.
translations.idiomatic: His father was Mian.

sentences.zh: 蕡寳歴二年進士擢第。

translations.literal: Fen passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Baoli.
translations.idiomatic: Fen passed the jinshi examination in 826.

sentences.zh: 博學善屬文，尤精左氏春秋。

translations.literal: Broadly learned and skilled in composition, he was especially expert in Mr. Zuo's Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly learned and skilled in composition, he was especially expert in Mr. Zuo's Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 與朋友交，好談王霸大畧，耿介嫉惡，言及世務，慨然有澄清之志。

translations.literal: In friendship he loved to discuss grand strategies of kingship and hegemony; upright and hating evil, when he spoke of public affairs he would sigh with the resolve to bring clarity.
translations.idiomatic: In friendship he loved to discuss grand strategies of kingship and hegemony; upright and hating evil, when he spoke of public affairs he would sigh with the resolve to bring clarity.

sentences.zh: 自元和末，閽寺權盛，握兵宮闈，橫制天下，天子廢立，由其可否，干撓庶政。

translations.literal: From the end of Yuanhe, eunuch power flourished; they held troops within the palace, controlled the realm by force, and whether the Son of Heaven was deposed or enthroned depended on their assent, as they interfered in all government.
translations.idiomatic: From the end of Yuanhe, eunuch power flourished; they held troops within the palace, controlled the realm by force, and whether the Son of Heaven was deposed or enthroned depended on their assent, as they interfered in all government.

sentences.zh: 當時目為南北司，愛惡相攻，有同水火。

translations.literal: At the time they were called the Northern and Southern Offices; love and hate attacked one another like fire and water.
translations.idiomatic: At the time they were called the Northern and Southern Offices; love and hate attacked one another like fire and water.

sentences.zh: 蕡草澤中居常憤惋。

translations.literal: Living in obscurity, Fen was constantly indignant and resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Living in obscurity, Fen was constantly indignant and resentful.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，恭儉求理，太和二年策試賢良曰：朕聞古先哲王之理也，玄黙無為，端拱思道，陶民心以居簡，凝日用而不宰，厚下以立本，推誠而建中。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenzong took the throne, reverent and frugal in seeking good order, in the second year of Taihe the examination for worthy and good men said, "I have heard that the governance of ancient sage-kings was darkly silent and non-active; seated upright they pondered the Way, molded the people's hearts to dwell in simplicity, concentrated daily use without interfering, enriched those below to establish the root, and extended sincerity to build the center."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenzong took the throne, reverent and frugal in seeking good order, in 828 the examination for worthy and good men said, I have heard that the governance of ancient sage-kings was darkly silent and non-active; seated upright they pondered the Way, molded the people's hearts to dwell in simplicity, concentrated daily use without interfering, enriched those below to establish the root, and extended sincerity to build the center.

sentences.zh: 是天人通，隂陽和，俗躋仁壽，物無疵癘。

translations.literal: Then Heaven and man were in communication, yin and yang were harmonious, custom reached benevolence and longevity, and things had no blemish or pestilence.
translations.idiomatic: Then Heaven and man were in communication, yin and yang were harmonious, custom reached benevolence and longevity, and things had no blemish or pestilence.

sentences.zh: 噫，盛徳之所臻，夐乎莫可及也。

translations.literal: Alas, what supreme virtue reaches is far beyond compare.
translations.idiomatic: Alas, what supreme virtue reaches is far beyond compare.

sentences.zh: 三代令王，質文迭䆒，百偽滋熾，風流寖微，自漢而降，定徴蓋寡。

translations.literal: The worthy kings of the Three Dynasties alternated substance and ornament; a hundred falsities grew fierce, refined custom gradually declined; from Han downward, fixed signs were few indeed.
translations.idiomatic: The worthy kings of the Three Dynasties alternated substance and ornament; a hundred falsities grew fierce, refined custom gradually declined; from Han downward, fixed signs were few indeed.

sentences.zh: 朕顧惟昧道，祗荷丕構，奉若謨訓，不敢怠荒。

translations.literal: I reflect that my understanding of the Way is dim; I reverently bear the great edifice, follow the instructions, and dare not be idle or negligent.
translations.idiomatic: I reflect that my understanding of the Way is dim; I reverently bear the great edifice, follow the instructions, and dare not be idle or negligent.

sentences.zh: 任賢惕厲，宵衣旰食，詎追三五之遐軌，庻紹祖宗之鴻緒。

translations.literal: Employing the worthy with vigilance, dressing at dawn and eating at dusk, how can I not pursue the distant tracks of the Three and Five, that I may continue the grand line of the ancestors?
translations.idiomatic: Employing the worthy with vigilance, dressing at dawn and eating at dusk, how can I not pursue the distant tracks of the Three and Five, that I may continue the grand line of the ancestors?

sentences.zh: 而心有所未逹，行有所未孚，由中及外，闕政斯廣。

translations.literal: Yet in my heart there are things not attained, in my conduct things not trusted; from center to outer reaches, neglected governance is wide.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in my heart there are things not attained, in my conduct things not trusted; from center to outer reaches, neglected governance is wide.

sentences.zh: 是以人不率化，氣或堙厄，災旱竟歲，播植愆時。

translations.literal: Therefore people do not follow transformation; qi sometimes is blocked in distress; drought and disaster last the whole year; planting misses its season.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore people do not follow transformation; qi sometimes is blocked in distress; drought and disaster last the whole year; planting misses its season.

sentences.zh: 國廪罕蓄，乏九年之儲；

translations.literal: The state granaries rarely store; there is a lack of nine years' reserves;
translations.idiomatic: The state granaries rarely store; there is a lack of nine years' reserves;

sentences.zh: 吏道多端，微三載之績。

translations.literal: The way of officials is many-branched; the achievement of three years' service is slight.
translations.idiomatic: The way of officials is many-branched; the achievement of three years' service is slight.

sentences.zh: 京師，諸夏之本也，将以觀理，而豪猾時踰檢；

translations.literal: The capital is the root of all the Xia; I intend to observe governance there, yet the powerful and cunning sometimes overstep bounds;
translations.idiomatic: The capital is the root of all the Xia; I intend to observe governance there, yet the powerful and cunning sometimes overstep bounds;

sentences.zh: 太學，明教之源也，期於變風，而生徒多惰業。

translations.literal: The Imperial Academy is the source of enlightened teaching; I expect to change custom there, yet students are mostly idle in their studies.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Academy is the source of enlightened teaching; I expect to change custom there, yet students are mostly idle in their studies.

sentences.zh: 列郡在乎頒條，而干禁或未絕；

translations.literal: Prefectures depend on promulgating regulations, yet violations of prohibitions are not yet ended;
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures depend on promulgating regulations, yet violations of prohibitions are not yet ended;

sentences.zh: 百工在乎按度，而滛巧或未衰。

translations.literal: The hundred crafts depend on measuring standards, yet licentious craft has not yet declined.
translations.idiomatic: The hundred crafts depend on measuring standards, yet licentious craft has not yet declined.

sentences.zh: 俗墮風靡，積訛成蠧。

translations.literal: Custom falls and the wind scatters; accumulated error becomes pest.
translations.idiomatic: Custom falls and the wind scatters; accumulated error becomes pest.

sentences.zh: 其擇官濟理也，聽人以言，則枝葉難辨；

translations.literal: In selecting officials to aid governance, if one listens to people's words, branches and leaves are hard to distinguish;
translations.idiomatic: In selecting officials to aid governance, if one listens to people's words, branches and leaves are hard to distinguish;

sentences.zh: 御下以法，則耻格不形。

translations.literal: In governing subordinates by law, shame and correction do not appear.
translations.idiomatic: In governing subordinates by law, shame and correction do not appear.

sentences.zh: 其阜財發號也，生之寡而食之衆，煩於令而鮮於理。

translations.literal: In enriching wealth and issuing orders, those born are few and those who eat are many; orders are troublesome while governance is scarce.
translations.idiomatic: In enriching wealth and issuing orders, those born are few and those who eat are many; orders are troublesome while governance is scarce.

sentences.zh: 思所以䆒此繆盭，致之治平，兹心浩然，若渉泉水。

translations.literal: I think how to untie these knots and errors and bring about ordered peace; this heart is vast, as if wading a spring stream.
translations.idiomatic: I think how to untie these knots and errors and bring about ordered peace; this heart is vast, as if wading a spring stream.

sentences.zh: 故前詔有司，博延群彦，佇啓宿懵，冀臻時雍。

translations.literal: Therefore I previously ordered the offices to broadly extend eminent men, await the opening of long-held confusion, and hope to reach timely harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I previously ordered the offices to broadly extend eminent men, await the opening of long-held confusion, and hope to reach timely harmony.

sentences.zh: 子大夫識逹古今，明於康濟，造廷待問，副朕虛懷。

translations.literal: You gentlemen know past and present and are clear on bringing relief; come to court and await questioning to match my open mind.
translations.idiomatic: You gentlemen know past and present and are clear on bringing relief; come to court and await questioning to match my open mind.

sentences.zh: 必當箴主之闕，辨政之疵，明綱條之致紊，稽富庶之所急。

translations.literal: You must admonish the ruler's faults, distinguish flaws in governance, clarify what causes laws and regulations to fall into disorder, and examine what the prosperous and numerous urgently need.
translations.idiomatic: You must admonish the ruler's faults, distinguish flaws in governance, clarify what causes laws and regulations to fall into disorder, and examine what the prosperous and numerous urgently need.

sentences.zh: 何施斯革於前弊，何澤斯惠乎下土，何脩而理古可近，何道而和氣克充，推之本源，著於條對。

translations.literal: What measure will reform former abuses? What grace will benefit the people below? What cultivation will bring near the governance of antiquity? What Way will fully fill harmonious qi? Trace to the root source and set forth in numbered replies.
translations.idiomatic: What measure will reform former abuses? What grace will benefit the people below? What cultivation will bring near the governance of antiquity? What Way will fully fill harmonious qi? Trace to the root source and set forth in numbered replies.

sentences.zh: 至於夷吾輕重之權，孰輔於理；

translations.literal: As for Guan Zhong's weighty and light authority, what aids governance?
translations.idiomatic: As for Guan Zhong's weighty and light authority, what aids governance?

sentences.zh: 嚴尤底定之䇿，孰叶於時；

translations.literal: As for Yan You's plan to settle the frontier, what fits the times?
translations.idiomatic: As for Yan You's plan to settle the frontier, what fits the times?

sentences.zh: 元凱之考課何先；

translations.literal: In Yuankai's examination of achievement, what comes first?
translations.idiomatic: In Yuankai's examination of achievement, what comes first?

sentences.zh: 叔子之克平何務。

translations.literal: In Shujizi's task of pacification, what is the business?
translations.idiomatic: In Shujizi's task of pacification, what is the business?

sentences.zh: 推此龜鏡，擇乎中庸，期在洽聞，朕將親覽。

translations.literal: Push this mirror of tortoise shell; choose the mean; expect comprehensive knowledge—I shall personally review.
translations.idiomatic: Push this mirror of tortoise shell; choose the mean; expect comprehensive knowledge—I shall personally review.

sentences.zh: 時對策者百餘人，所對止循常務，唯蕡切論黄門太横，将危宗社，對曰：臣誠不佞，有匡國致君之術，無位而不得行；

translations.literal: At the time more than a hundred men answered the examination; their replies merely followed routine affairs. Only Fen sharply discussed the Yellow Gate's excessive power, which would endanger the altars of state. He replied, Your subject is truly unworthy, yet has the art of stabilizing the state and serving the ruler, but no position from which to carry it out;
translations.idiomatic: At the time more than a hundred men answered the examination; their replies merely followed routine affairs. Only Fen sharply discussed the Yellow Gate's excessive power, which would endanger the altars of state. He replied, Your subject is truly unworthy, yet has the art of stabilizing the state and serving the ruler, but no position from which to carry it out;

sentences.zh: 有犯顏敢諫之心，無路而不得進。

translations.literal: he has the heart to offend the countenance and dare remonstrate, but no road by which to advance.
translations.idiomatic: he has the heart to offend the countenance and dare remonstrate, but no road by which to advance.

sentences.zh: 但懷憤鬱抑，思有時而一發耳。

translations.literal: He only harbors indignant depression, thinking to release it at some moment.
translations.idiomatic: He only harbors indignant depression, thinking to release it at some moment.

sentences.zh: 常欲與庶人議於道，商旅謗於市，得通上聽，一悟主心，雖被妖言之罪，無所悔焉。

translations.literal: He has often wished to discuss with common people on the road and have travelers complain in the market, that it might reach the ruler's hearing and awaken the ruler's heart in one stroke—even if punished for perverse speech, he would not regret it.
translations.idiomatic: He has often wished to discuss with common people on the road and have travelers complain in the market, that it might reach the ruler's hearing and awaken the ruler's heart in one stroke—even if punished for perverse speech, he would not regret it.

sentences.zh: 況逢陛下以至德嗣興，以大明垂照，詢求過闕，咨訪謨猷，制詔中外，舉直言極諫者。

translations.literal: Moreover, encountering Your Majesty succeeding with supreme virtue and shining with great brilliance, seeking faults and oversights and consulting on plans, issuing edicts throughout the realm calling for forthright speech and extreme remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, encountering Your Majesty succeeding with supreme virtue and shining with great brilliance, seeking faults and oversights and consulting on plans, issuing edicts throughout the realm calling for forthright speech and extreme remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 臣旣辱斯舉，專承大問，敢不悉意以言。

translations.literal: Your subject has been honored with this summons and specially receives this great questioning—how dare he not speak with full intent?
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has been honored with this summons and specially receives this great questioning—how dare he not speak with full intent?

sentences.zh: 至於上之所忌，時之所禁，權倖之所諱惡，有司之所與奪，臣愚不識。

translations.literal: As for what the ruler fears, what the times forbid, what favorites hate, and what offices grant or withhold, your subject in his foolishness does not know.
translations.idiomatic: As for what the ruler fears, what the times forbid, what favorites hate, and what offices grant or withhold, your subject in his foolishness does not know.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下少加優容，不使聖朝有讜直而受戮者，乃天下之幸也。

translations.literal: I humbly hope Your Majesty will grant a little indulgence and not let the sagely court have forthright men who are punished—this would be the fortune of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly hope Your Majesty will grant a little indulgence and not let the sagely court have forthright men who are punished—this would be the fortune of the realm.

sentences.zh: 謹昧死以對。

translations.literal: I respectfully risk death in reply.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully risk death in reply.

sentences.zh: 伏惟聖策，有思先古之理，念玄默之化，將欲通天人以齊俗，和陰陽以煦物，見陛下慕道之深也。

translations.literal: I humbly consider the sagely question: there is thought of the governance of ancient sages and remembrance of darkly silent transformation, intending to join Heaven and man to equalize custom and harmonize yin and yang to warm things—this shows how deeply Your Majesty cherishes the Way.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly consider the sagely question: there is thought of the governance of ancient sages and remembrance of darkly silent transformation, intending to join Heaven and man to equalize custom and harmonize yin and yang to warm things—this shows how deeply Your Majesty cherishes the Way.

sentences.zh: 臣以為哲王之理，其則不遠，惟陛下致之之道何如爾。

translations.literal: Your subject thinks the governance of a wise king—the rule is not far off; it depends only on how Your Majesty brings it about.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject thinks the governance of a wise king—the rule is not far off; it depends only on how Your Majesty brings it about.

sentences.zh: 伏惟聖策，有祗荷丕構而不敢荒寧，奉若謨訓而罔有怠忽，見陛下憂勞之志也。

translations.literal: I humbly consider the sagely question: there is reverently bearing the great edifice without daring idle ease, following instructions without negligence—this shows Your Majesty's resolve of anxious labor.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly consider the sagely question: there is reverently bearing the great edifice without daring idle ease, following instructions without negligence—this shows Your Majesty's resolve of anxious labor.

sentences.zh: 若夫任賢惕厲，宵衣旰食，宜黜左右之纖佞，進股肱之大臣；

translations.literal: As for employing the worthy with vigilance and dressing at dawn and eating at dusk, one should dismiss the slender sycophants at the ruler's side and advance the great ministers who are the ruler's limbs;
translations.idiomatic: As for employing the worthy with vigilance and dressing at dawn and eating at dusk, one should dismiss the slender sycophants at the ruler's side and advance the great ministers who are the ruler's limbs;

sentences.zh: 若夫追蹤三五，紹復祖宗，宜鑒前古之興亡，明當時之成敗。

translations.literal: As for pursuing the Three and Five and restoring the ancestors, one should mirror the rise and fall of former antiquity and clarify the success and failure of the present time.
translations.idiomatic: As for pursuing the Three and Five and restoring the ancestors, one should mirror the rise and fall of former antiquity and clarify the success and failure of the present time.

sentences.zh: 心有所未達，以下情塞而不得上通；

translations.literal: Where the heart has not attained, it is because feelings below are blocked and cannot reach above;
translations.idiomatic: Where the heart has not attained, it is because feelings below are blocked and cannot reach above;

sentences.zh: 行有所未孚，以上澤壅而不得下浹。

translations.literal: Your conduct has points it has not won trust; above, favor is dammed and cannot flow downward to soak all.
translations.idiomatic: Your conduct has not won full trust; above, your grace is dammed and cannot reach the people below.

sentences.zh: 欲人之化也，在脩己以先之；

translations.literal: If one wishes people to be transformed, one must cultivate oneself first;
translations.idiomatic: If one wishes people to be transformed, one must cultivate oneself first;

sentences.zh: 欲氣之和也，在遂性以導之。

translations.literal: if one wishes qi to be harmonious, one must follow nature and guide it.
translations.idiomatic: if one wishes qi to be harmonious, one must follow nature and guide it.

sentences.zh: 救災患在致乎精誠，廣播植在視乎食力。

translations.literal: Relieving disaster and drought lies in utmost sincerity; broad planting lies in seeing to the people's labor.
translations.idiomatic: Relieving disaster and drought lies in utmost sincerity; broad planting lies in seeing to the people's labor.

sentences.zh: 國廩罕蓄，本乎冗食尚繁；

translations.literal: That the state granaries rarely store lies in redundant eaters still being numerous;
translations.idiomatic: That the state granaries rarely store lies in redundant eaters still being numerous;

sentences.zh: 吏道多端，本乎選用失當。

translations.literal: The official way has many divisions; fundamentally it lies in inappropriate appointment and employment.
translations.idiomatic: The bureaucratic disorder has many branches, but at root it comes from appointing the wrong men.

sentences.zh: 豪猾踰制，由中外之法殊；

translations.literal: Overbearing ruffians overstep regulations, because the laws of the inner and outer courts differ;
translations.idiomatic: Overbearing wrongdoers exceed all bounds because the rules of court and provinces no longer align;

sentences.zh: 生徒墮業，由學校之官廢。

translations.literal: Students fall from their studies, because the officials of the schools have been abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Students neglect their studies because the schools have been left without proper officers.

sentences.zh: 列郡干禁，由授任非人；

translations.literal: Commandery after commandery violate prohibitions, because appointments are given to unfit men;
translations.idiomatic: Prefecture after prefecture breaks the law because unworthy men hold office;

sentences.zh: 百工淫巧，由制度不立。

translations.literal: The hundred crafts pursue extravagant cleverness, because institutions are not established.
translations.idiomatic: Artisans chase wasteful luxury because proper standards have never been fixed.

sentences.zh: 伏以聖策，有擇官濟理之心，阜財發號之歎，見陛下教化之本也。

translations.literal: Your subject observes that in the sage edict there is the intent to select officials to aid governance and the sigh over enriching wealth and issuing commands — this shows Your Majesty's foundation of instruction and transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Your decree shows Your Majesty's intent to appoint the right officials and your concern to strengthen public finance — the very roots of good governance.

sentences.zh: 且進人以行，則枝葉安有難別乎？

translations.literal: Moreover, if one advances men by conduct, then how could branches and leaves be hard to distinguish?
translations.idiomatic: If promotions were based on character, how could the worthy and unworthy be hard to tell apart?

sentences.zh: 防下以禮，則耻格安有不形乎？

translations.literal: If one restrains subordinates by ritual, then how could the shame of correction fail to appear?
translations.idiomatic: If subordinates were governed by ritual, would shame not restrain wrongdoing plainly enough?

sentences.zh: 念生寡而食衆，可罷斥惰游；

translations.literal: Reflecting that producers are few while consumers are many, one may dismiss the idle and the wandering;
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that producers are few and dependents many, dismiss the idle and the dissolute;

sentences.zh: 念令煩而理鮮，要察其行否。

translations.literal: Reflecting that commands are numerous while good order is scarce, the essential thing is to examine whether conduct is sound or not.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing how laws multiply while effective rule grows scarce, examine officials' conduct strictly.

sentences.zh: 博延群彥，願陛下必納其言；

translations.literal: Broadly extending to gather worthy talents — I hope Your Majesty will surely accept their words;
translations.idiomatic: You have summoned worthy men widely; I pray Your Majesty will heed what they say.

sentences.zh: 造廷待問，則小臣安敢愛死。

translations.literal: Summoned to court to await questioning — how would this humble subject dare spare his life?
translations.idiomatic: Called to court to answer — how could your humble servant hold back, even at the cost of his life?

sentences.zh: 伏以聖策，有求賢箴闕之言，審政辨疵之念，見陛下咨訪之勤也。

translations.literal: Your subject observes that in the sage edict there are words of seeking the worthy and admonishing shortcomings, and thoughts of examining government and distinguishing flaws — this shows Your Majesty's diligence in consultation and inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Your decree shows Your Majesty's desire to seek worthy men, admonish your own faults, and examine policy for defects — proof of your earnest consultation.

sentences.zh: 遂小臣屏姦豪之志，則弊革於前；

translations.literal: Then this humble subject's resolve to shut out wicked magnates would reform abuses beforehand;
translations.idiomatic: Then your servant's resolve to drive out wicked magnates would reform abuses before they spread;

sentences.zh: 守陛下念康濟之心，則惠敷於下。

translations.literal: Upholding Your Majesty's mind intent on peace and relief, then favor would spread below.
translations.idiomatic: Uphold Your Majesty's concern for the people's welfare, and blessings would reach every level of society.

sentences.zh: 邪正之道分，則理古可近；

translations.literal: If the ways of the wicked and the upright are separated, then governing as in antiquity may be approached;
translations.idiomatic: Separate the wicked from the upright, and the governance of antiquity may be approached again;

sentences.zh: 禮樂之方著，而和氣克充。

translations.literal: If the methods of ritual and music are made manifest, then harmonious qi can fully fill the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Establish ritual and music in their proper place, and harmonious order will prevail throughout the land.

sentences.zh: 至若夷吾之法，非皇王之權；

translations.literal: As for the methods of Guan Zhong, they are not the authority of an august king;
translations.idiomatic: As for Guan Zhong's methods, they are not the prerogative of a true sovereign;

sentences.zh: 嚴尤所陳，無最上之策。

translations.literal: What Yan You presented offers no supreme policy.
translations.idiomatic: What Yan You proposed was no policy of the highest order.

sentences.zh: 元凱之所先，不若唐、虞之考績；

translations.literal: What Yi Yin and Yu Ya put first is not equal to the performance evaluation of Yao and Shun;
translations.idiomatic: The priorities of Yi Yin and Yu Ya cannot match Yao and Shun's system of evaluating merit;

sentences.zh: 叔子之所務，不若重華之舞干。

translations.literal: What Lu Meng made his task is not equal to Shun's dancing with shields and axes.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Meng's preoccupations cannot compare with Emperor Shun's triumph over the Miao through ritual rather than arms;

sentences.zh: 且俱非大德之中庸，未為上聖之龜鑑，何足以為陛下道之哉！

translations.literal: Moreover, all alike fall short of the golden mean of great virtue and are not the tortoise mirror of the highest sage — how could they suffice as models for Your Majesty!
translations.idiomatic: None of these measures embodies the golden mean of supreme virtue or offers the sure mirror of the sage — how could they serve as Your Majesty's guide!

sentences.zh: 或有以繫安危之機，兆存亡之變者，臣請披瀝肝膽，為陛下別白而重言之。

translations.literal: If there are matters that bear on the pivot of safety and danger and foreshadow the turn of survival and ruin, your subject asks leave to lay bare his liver and gall and speak them out separately and emphatically for Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: On matters that touch the pivot of safety and danger and foreshadow survival or ruin, I beg leave to lay bare my heart and speak plainly once more.

sentences.zh: 臣前所謂「哲王之理，其則不遠」者，在陛下慎思之，力行之，終始不懈而已。

translations.literal: What your subject said earlier — "The governance of a wise king: its standard is not far off" — lies simply in Your Majesty's thinking carefully, acting forcefully, and never slackening from beginning to end.
translations.idiomatic: What I said earlier — "The governance of a wise king: its standard is not far to seek" — depends only on Your Majesty's careful thought, resolute action, and unwavering persistence from start to finish.

sentences.zh: 臣謹按春秋：「元者，氣之始也；

translations.literal: Your subject respectfully cites the Spring and Autumn Annals: "Yuan is the beginning of qi;
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully cite the Spring and Autumn Annals: "Yuan is the beginning of vital force;

sentences.zh: 春者，歲之始也。」

translations.literal: Spring is the beginning of the year."
translations.idiomatic: Spring is the beginning of the year."

sentences.zh: 春秋以元加於歲，以春加於王，明王者當奉若天道，以謹其始也。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals adds yuan to the year and spring to the king — making clear that the king ought to revere and follow Heaven's Way in being careful at the beginning.
translations.idiomatic: The Annals places yuan before the year and spring before the king's name, showing that a ruler must honor Heaven's Way and be scrupulous at the outset.

sentences.zh: 又舉時以終歲，舉月以終時，春秋雖無事，必書首月以存時，明王者當奉若天道，以謹其終也。

translations.literal: It also takes the season to end the year and the month to end the season; though the Annals records no event, it always writes the first month to preserve the season — making clear that the king ought to revere and follow Heaven's Way in being careful at the end.
translations.idiomatic: It marks the season to close the year and the month to close the season; even when nothing happens, it always records the first month to preserve the calendar — showing that a ruler must honor Heaven's Way and be scrupulous to the end.

sentences.zh: 王者動作終始必法於天者，以其運行不息也。

translations.literal: The reason a king's actions from beginning to end must take Heaven as model is that Heaven's movement never ceases.
translations.idiomatic: A king's conduct from beginning to end must follow Heaven's model, for Heaven never ceases its course.

sentences.zh: 陛下旣能謹其始，又能謹其終，懋而脩之，勤而行之，則可以執契而居簡，無為而不宰，廣立本之大業，崇建中之盛德矣。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty can be careful at the beginning and careful at the end, exert yourself in cultivating this and diligently carry it out, then you may hold the tally and dwell in simplicity, act without acting yet govern all, broadly establish the great enterprise of laying the foundation, and exalt the splendid virtue of the Jianzhong era.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty can be scrupulous at the beginning and at the end, cultivate this earnestly and act on it diligently, you may hold the tally of rule in tranquil simplicity, govern without force, broadly establish the foundation of the state, and restore the splendid virtue of the Jianzhong reign.

sentences.zh: 又安有三代循環之弊，而為百偽滋熾之漸乎？

translations.literal: How then could there still be the cyclical abuses of the Three Dynasties and the gradual growth of a hundred falsities!
translations.idiomatic: How then could the cyclical decay of the Three Dynasties return, or a hundred corruptions take root again!

sentences.zh: 臣故曰「惟陛下致之之道何如耳」。

translations.literal: Therefore your subject says, "It depends only on what path Your Majesty takes to achieve it."
translations.idiomatic: That is why I said, "It depends only on the path Your Majesty chooses to achieve it."

sentences.zh: 臣前所謂「若夫任賢惕厲，宵衣旰食，宜罷黜左右之纖佞，進股肱之大臣」者，實以陛下憂勞之至也。

translations.literal: What your subject said earlier — "As for employing the worthy with vigilance, rising before dawn and eating after dusk, you ought to dismiss the petty flatterers at your side and advance the chief ministers who are your right arm and thigh" — was truly because Your Majesty's worry and labor have reached their utmost.
translations.idiomatic: What I said earlier — "In employing the worthy with vigilance, rising before dawn and eating after dusk, you ought to dismiss the petty flatterers at your side and advance the chief ministers who are your right arm and thigh" — was truly because Your Majesty's worry and labor have reached their limit.

sentences.zh: 臣聞不宜憂而憂者，國必衰；

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that when one worries over what ought not to be worried over, the state must decline;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that when a ruler worries over the wrong things, the state must decline;

sentences.zh: 宜憂而不憂者，國必危。

translations.literal: When one fails to worry over what ought to be worried over, the state must be endangered.
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler fails to worry over what he ought to worry over, the state must be in peril.

sentences.zh: 今陛下不以國家存亡之事、社稷安危之策，而降於清問。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty does not bring down clear inquiry upon matters of the state's survival or ruin and policies for the altars' safety or danger.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Your Majesty has not addressed the questions of the state's survival and the altars' safety in your clear inquiry.

sentences.zh: 臣未知陛下以布衣之臣不足以定大計耶？

translations.literal: Your subject does not know whether Your Majesty thinks that a subject in plain cloth is insufficient to settle the great plan.
translations.idiomatic: I do not know whether Your Majesty thinks a common subject unfit to settle great affairs.

sentences.zh: 或萬機之勤，而聖慮有所未至耶？

translations.literal: Or whether amid the diligence of the myriad affairs, the sage consideration has not yet reached certain points?
translations.idiomatic: Or whether amid the press of ten thousand affairs your sage consideration has not yet reached the heart of the matter?

sentences.zh: 不然，何宜憂而不憂者乎？

translations.literal: If not, then why is this a case of failing to worry over what ought to be worried over?
translations.idiomatic: If not, why do you fail to worry over what you ought to worry over?

sentences.zh: 臣以為陛下宜先憂者，宮闈將變，社稷將危，天下將傾，海內將亂。

translations.literal: Your subject believes that what Your Majesty ought to worry about first is this: the inner palace is about to change, the altars of state are about to be endangered, the realm is about to topple, and within the seas disorder is about to break out.
translations.idiomatic: I believe Your Majesty's first concerns ought to be these: the inner palace is on the verge of upheaval, the altars of state are in danger, the realm is tottering, and turmoil is about to engulf the empire.

sentences.zh: 此四者，國家已然之兆，故臣謂聖慮宜先及之。

translations.literal: These four are already manifest signs of the state; therefore your subject says the sage consideration ought to reach them first.
translations.idiomatic: These four are already manifest signs of national crisis; therefore I say Your Majesty's concern ought to reach them first.

sentences.zh: 夫帝業旣艱難而成之，故不可容易而守之。

translations.literal: Since the imperial enterprise was achieved only through hardship, it cannot be guarded lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Since the imperial enterprise was won only through hardship, it cannot be held lightly.

sentences.zh: 昔太祖肇其基，高祖勤其績，太宗定其業，玄宗繼其明，至于陛下，二百有餘載矣。
