translations.literal: In the past Taizu laid its foundation, Gaozu toiled at its achievements, Taizong fixed its enterprise, and Xuanzong continued its brilliance; down to Your Majesty, more than two hundred years have passed.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu laid the foundation, Gaozu built on his work, Taizong secured the enterprise, and Xuanzong carried forward its brilliance; down to Your Majesty, more than two hundred years have passed.

sentences.zh: 其間明聖相因，憂亂繼作，未有不委用賢士，親近正人，而能紹興其徽烈者也。

translations.literal: In that interval sage rulers followed one another and worry and disorder arose in succession; never was there a case that did not entrust employment to worthy scholars, keep upright men near, and thereby continue and revive their splendid achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Through that span sage rulers succeeded one another and crises arose in turn; never once did a dynasty survive without entrusting power to worthy men, keeping upright counselors near, and thereby renewing its glory.

sentences.zh: 或一日不念，則顛覆大器，宗廟之耻，萬古為恨。

translations.literal: If for a single day one fails to reflect, then the great vessel is overturned — the shame of the ancestral temple becomes a regret for ten thousand ages.
translations.idiomatic: Neglect it for a single day and the great vessel is overturned — the shame of the ancestral temple becomes an eternal regret.

sentences.zh: 臣謹按春秋，人君之道在體元以居正，昔董仲舒為漢武帝言之略矣。

translations.literal: Your subject respectfully cites the Spring and Autumn Annals: the way of a ruler lies in embodying the origin and occupying the correct position; long ago Dong Zhongshu spoke of this to Emperor Wu of Han in outline.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully cite the Spring and Autumn Annals: the ruler's way lies in embodying the origin and holding the correct position — Dong Zhongshu explained this to Emperor Wu of Han long ago.

sentences.zh: 其所未盡者，臣得為陛下備而論之。

translations.literal: What he did not fully set forth, your subject may set out completely for Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: What he left unsaid, I may now set forth fully for Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 夫繼故必書即位，所以正其始也；

translations.literal: When one succeeds the former ruler, the accession must be recorded — this is to rectify the beginning;
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler succeeds his predecessor, the accession must be recorded — to set the beginning right;

sentences.zh: 終必書所終之地，所以正其終也。

translations.literal: At the end one must record the place where he ended — this is to rectify the end.
translations.idiomatic: At the end one must record where he died — to set the ending right.

sentences.zh: 故為君者，所發必正言，所履必正道，所居必正位，所近必正人。

translations.literal: Therefore for one who is ruler: what he issues must be upright words, what he treads must be the upright Way, where he dwells must be the upright position, and whom he keeps near must be upright men.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore a ruler must speak upright words, walk the upright path, occupy the rightful place, and keep upright men near.

sentences.zh: 臣又按春秋「閽弒吳子餘祭」，不書其君。

translations.literal: Your subject further cites the Spring and Autumn Annals: "The gate commander assassinated Prince Yu of Wu," and does not record him as ruler.
translations.idiomatic: I further cite the Spring and Autumn Annals: "The gate commander assassinated Prince Yu of Wu," and does not record him as ruler.

sentences.zh: 春秋譏其疏遠賢士，昵近刑人，有不君之道矣。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals rebukes him for keeping worthy scholars at a distance and drawing near to men of punishment — he had the way of one who is not a ruler.
translations.idiomatic: The Annals rebukes him for keeping worthy men at a distance and drawing near to executioners — he had ceased to be a true ruler.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下思祖宗開國之勤，念春秋繼故之誡。

translations.literal: Your subject humbly hopes Your Majesty will reflect on the toil of the founding ancestors and keep in mind the admonition of the Spring and Autumn Annals on succeeding the former ruler.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly urge Your Majesty to reflect on the founding ancestors' toil and heed the Annals' warning on succession.

sentences.zh: 將明法度之端，則發正言而履正道；

translations.literal: If you wish to clarify the beginning of law and institutions, then issue upright words and tread the upright Way;
translations.idiomatic: To clarify the foundations of law and order, speak upright words and walk the upright path;

sentences.zh: 將杜篡弒之漸，則居正位而近正人。

translations.literal: If you wish to cut off the gradual growth of usurpation and regicide, then occupy the correct position and keep upright men near.
translations.idiomatic: To choke off the drift toward regicide, hold the throne in dignity and keep honest men close.

sentences.zh: 遠刀鋸之賤，親骨鯁之直，輔相得以專其任，庶職得以守其官。

translations.literal: Keep far from the base of the knife and saw; be close to blunt, loyal remonstrators; let the chief ministers fully carry out their duties, and let the hundred offices keep to their posts.
translations.idiomatic: Banish the butcher's minions; cherish the blunt counselors who speak truth; let your chief ministers govern, and let every office do its work.

sentences.zh: 奈何以褻近五六人，總天下大政，外專陛下之命，內竊陛下之權，威懾朝廷，勢傾海內，群臣莫敢指其狀，天子不得制其心。

translations.literal: How can you let five or six lewd intimates hold all great government of the realm — outwardly monopolizing Your Majesty's commands, inwardly stealing Your Majesty's authority, awing the court with their power and tilting their influence across the seas, so that no minister dares point out their condition and the Son of Heaven cannot control their hearts?
translations.idiomatic: How can five or six favored intimates run the empire — issuing Your Majesty's orders in name while seizing your power in fact, awing the court and dominating the realm, so that no minister dares speak and the Son of Heaven cannot control them?

sentences.zh: 禍稔蕭牆，姦生帷幄，臣恐曹節、侯覽，復生於今日，此宮闈之所以將變也。

translations.literal: Disaster ripens within the palace walls; treachery is born inside the curtain. Your subject fears Cao Jie and Hou Lan are being reborn in our own day — this is why the inner palace is about to change.
translations.idiomatic: Disaster is ripening behind the palace walls; treachery is breeding within the curtained hall. I fear that Cao Jie and Hou Lan live again in our time — this is why the inner palace is on the verge of upheaval.

sentences.zh: 臣謹按春秋，魯定公元年春王不言正月者，春秋以其先君不得正其終，則後君不得正其始，故曰定無正也。

translations.literal: Your subject respectfully cites the Spring and Autumn Annals: in the first year of Duke Ding of Lu, in spring the king is recorded but the first month is not spoken — the Annals holds that because the former ruler could not end his reign properly, the later ruler could not begin his properly; therefore it says Duke Ding had no proper beginning.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully cite the Spring and Autumn Annals: in Duke Ding of Lu's first year, spring is recorded but the first month is not — because the former ruler could not end his reign properly, the successor could not begin his properly; hence the Annals says Duke Ding had no legitimate beginning.

sentences.zh: 今忠賢無腹心之奇，閽寺持廢立之權，陷先君不得正其終，致陛下不得正其始。

translations.literal: Now loyal worthies have no place to lodge their hearts; eunuch gate commanders hold the power to depose and establish; they trapped the late emperor so that he could not end his reign properly, and they have caused Your Majesty not to begin yours properly.
translations.idiomatic: Today loyal ministers have nowhere to place their trust; eunuch commanders hold the power to make and unmake emperors. They prevented your predecessor from ending his reign in peace and have kept you from beginning yours in legitimacy.

sentences.zh: 況皇儲未建，郊祀未脩，將相之職不歸，名分之宜不定，此社稷之所以將危也。

translations.literal: Moreover the crown heir is not established, the suburban sacrifices are not performed, the duties of generals and ministers are not returned to their proper holders, and the proprieties of rank and title are not fixed — this is why the altars of state are about to be endangered.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover no crown heir has been appointed, the suburban sacrifices have not been performed, the roles of generals and ministers remain unsettled, and rank and title are in confusion — this is why the altars of state are in danger.

sentences.zh: 臣謹按春秋「王札子殺召伯、毛伯」。

translations.literal: Your subject respectfully cites the Spring and Autumn Annals: "Wang Zhaozi killed the Earl of Shao and the Earl of Mao"
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully cite the Spring and Autumn Annals: "Wang Zhaozi killed the Earl of Shao and the Earl of Mao"

sentences.zh: 春秋之義，兩下相殺不書。

translations.literal: The principle of the Spring and Autumn Annals is that when two parties kill each other it is not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: The Annals' principle is that mutual killings between equals are not recorded.

sentences.zh: 而此書者，重其專王命也。

translations.literal: Yet this is recorded — to emphasize his usurpation of the king's command.
translations.idiomatic: Yet this case is recorded — to emphasize his usurpation of the royal command.

sentences.zh: 且天之所授者在君，君之所授者在命。

translations.literal: Moreover, what Heaven confers rests with the ruler; what the ruler confers rests with his command.
translations.idiomatic: What Heaven bestows rests with the ruler; what the ruler bestows rests with his command.

sentences.zh: 操其命而失之者，是不君也；

translations.literal: One who holds the command yet loses it — such a one is not a ruler;
translations.idiomatic: One who holds the command yet loses it is no ruler;

sentences.zh: 侵其命而專之者，是不臣也。

translations.literal: One who encroaches on the command and monopolizes it — such a one is not a minister.
translations.idiomatic: One who encroaches on the command and monopolizes it is no minister.

sentences.zh: 君不君，臣不臣，此天下所以將傾也。

translations.literal: Ruler not acting as ruler, minister not acting as minister — this is why the realm is about to topple.
translations.idiomatic: When ruler and minister no longer act as they should, the realm is about to topple — this is why.

sentences.zh: 臣謹按春秋，晉趙鞅以晉陽之兵叛入于晉。

translations.literal: Your subject respectfully cites the Spring and Autumn Annals: Zhao Yang of Jin led the troops of Jinyang in rebellion and entered Jin.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully cite the Spring and Autumn Annals: Zhao Yang of Jin led the troops of Jinyang in rebellion against the state.

sentences.zh: 今威柄凌夷，藩臣跋扈。

translations.literal: Now imperial authority declines day by day, and the frontier lords are arrogant and domineering.
translations.idiomatic: Today sovereign power erodes daily, while the military commissioners grow insolent on their borders.

sentences.zh: 或有不達人臣之節，首亂者以安君為名；

translations.literal: Some who do not understand a subject's propriety take the lead in disorder in the name of securing the ruler;
translations.idiomatic: Some who know nothing of a subject's duty take the lead in rebellion in the name of saving the throne;

sentences.zh: 不究春秋之微，稱兵者以逐惡為義。

translations.literal: Without investigating the subtle meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals, those who raise armies call it righteous to drive out the wicked.
translations.idiomatic: Without heeding the Annals' subtle warnings, those who raise armies claim righteousness in driving out evil.

sentences.zh: 則政刑不由乎天子，攻伐必自於諸侯，此海內之所以將亂也。

translations.literal: Then government and punishments no longer proceed from the Son of Heaven, and attacks and campaigns necessarily begin with the feudal lords — this is why within the seas disorder is about to break out.
translations.idiomatic: Then government and punishment no longer come from the throne, and war begins with the regional lords — this is why turmoil is about to engulf the empire.

sentences.zh: 又樊噲排闥而雪涕，爰盎當車以抗詞，京房發憤以殞身，竇武不顧而畢命，此皆陛下明知之矣。

translations.literal: Moreover Fan Kuai pushed open the door in tears, Yuan Ang blocked the carriage with bold words, Jing Fang gave vent to indignation and lost his life, and Dou Wu paid no heed to danger and ended his life — all this Your Majesty clearly knows.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Kuai burst through the door in tears; Yuan Ang blocked the carriage with bold remonstrance; Jing Fang spoke in righteous anger and lost his life; Dou Wu ignored all danger and died for his cause — Your Majesty knows all this well.

sentences.zh: 臣謹按春秋，晉狐射姑殺陽處父。

translations.literal: Your subject respectfully cites the Spring and Autumn Annals: Hu Shegu of Jin killed Yang Chufu.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully cite the Spring and Autumn Annals: Hu Shegu of Jin killed Yang Chufu.

sentences.zh: 襄公不能固陰重之機，處父所以及戕賊之禍，故春秋非之。

translations.literal: Duke Xiang could not secure the hidden, weighty pivot; therefore Chufu met the disaster of slaughter — for this the Spring and Autumn Annals rebukes him.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Xiang failed to secure the hidden levers of power, and Chufu met a violent death — for this the Annals rebukes him.

sentences.zh: 夫上漏其情，則下不敢盡意；

translations.literal: When the ruler leaks his feelings, then those below dare not fully express their intent;
translations.idiomatic: When the ruler reveals his mind, those below dare not speak their full mind;

sentences.zh: 上泄其事，則下不敢盡言。

translations.literal: When the ruler divulges their affairs, then those below dare not fully speak.
translations.idiomatic: When the ruler leaks what is said to him, those below dare not speak freely.

sentences.zh: 傳有「造膝」「詭辭」之文，易有「殺身」「害成」之戒。

translations.literal: The Commentary has the phrases "approaching the knee" and "deceptive words"; the Changes has the warnings "sacrificing one's life" and "ruining success."
translations.idiomatic: The Commentary speaks of "approaching the knee" and "deceptive words"; the Changes has the warnings "sacrificing one's life" and "ruining success."

sentences.zh: 今公卿大臣，非不能為陛下言之，慮陛下必不能用之。

translations.literal: Now the chief ministers and great officials are not unable to speak to Your Majesty — they fear Your Majesty will surely not employ what they say.
translations.idiomatic: Today's chief ministers are not unable to speak — they fear Your Majesty will not act on what they say.

sentences.zh: 陛下旣忽之而不用，必洩其言；

translations.literal: If Your Majesty neglects their words and does not employ them, you will surely leak what they say;
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty ignores their counsel, you will inevitably leak what they say;

sentences.zh: 臣下旣言之而不行，必嬰其禍。

translations.literal: If subjects have spoken yet their words are not carried out, they will surely meet disaster.
translations.idiomatic: If ministers speak and nothing is done, they will surely suffer for it.

sentences.zh: 適足以鉗直臣之口，重奸臣之威。

translations.literal: This is exactly enough to clamp shut the mouths of upright ministers and increase the authority of wicked ministers.
translations.idiomatic: This only silences upright ministers and strengthens wicked ones.

sentences.zh: 是以欲盡其言，則起失身之懼；

translations.literal: Therefore if they wish to speak fully, the fear of losing their lives arises;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore if they wish to speak fully, they fear for their lives;

sentences.zh: 欲盡其意，則有害成之憂。

translations.literal: If they wish to express their intent fully, then the worry of ruining the achievement arises.
translations.idiomatic: If they wish to speak their full mind, they fear ruining what good might yet be done.

sentences.zh: 故徘徊鬱塞，以俟陛下感悟，然後盡其啟沃耳。

translations.literal: Therefore they hesitate and are blocked and depressed, waiting for Your Majesty's awakening — only then will they fully offer their nourishing counsel.
translations.idiomatic: So they hesitate and hold back, waiting for Your Majesty to understand — only then will they offer their full counsel.

sentences.zh: 陛下何不以聽朝之餘，時御便殿，召當時賢相與舊德老臣，訪持變扶危之謀，求定傾救亂之術。

translations.literal: Why does Your Majesty not, in the intervals after hearing court affairs, from time to time enter the informal hall, summon the worthy chancellors of the day and old ministers of established virtue, and inquire after plans to hold off change and support what is endangered, and seek methods to set right what is toppling and rescue what is in disorder?
translations.idiomatic: Why not, between sessions of court, from time to time enter the informal hall, summon the worthy chancellors and venerable ministers of the day, and ask their plans for holding off disaster and restoring order?

sentences.zh: 塞陰邪之路，屏褻狎之臣，制侵凌迫脅之心，復門戶掃除之役，戒其所宜戒，憂其所宜憂。

translations.literal: Block the paths of hidden wickedness; remove lewd and familiar ministers; restrain the mind that encroaches, oppresses, and coerces; restore the work of clearing the gate and courtyard; warn against what ought to be warned against; worry over what ought to be worried over.
translations.idiomatic: Block the paths of hidden evil; remove favored intimates; restrain those who encroach and coerce; restore the work of purging faction; warn against what must be warned against; worry over what must be worried over.

sentences.zh: 旣不能治於前，當治於後；

translations.literal: If you could not govern properly before, you ought to govern properly afterward;
translations.idiomatic: If you could not set things right before, set them right now;

sentences.zh: 旣不能正其始，當正其終。

translations.literal: If you could not rectify the beginning, you ought to rectify the end.
translations.idiomatic: If you could not set the beginning right, set the ending right.

sentences.zh: 則可以虔奉典謨，克承丕構，終任賢之効，無旰食之憂矣。

translations.literal: Then you may reverently uphold the canonical plans, fully inherit the great enterprise, ultimately achieve the effect of employing the worthy, and be free of the worry of eating after dusk.
translations.idiomatic: Then you may reverently uphold the canonical models, fully inherit the great enterprise, achieve the fruits of employing worthy men, and be free of the worry of toiling past dusk.

sentences.zh: 臣前所謂「若夫追蹤三五，紹復祖宗，宜鑒前古之興亡，明當時之成敗」者。

translations.literal: What your subject said earlier — "As for following in the tracks of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors and continuing and restoring the ancestors, you ought to take as mirror the rise and fall of former ages and clarify the success and failure of the present day" —
translations.idiomatic: What I said earlier — "To follow the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors and restore the ancestors' legacy, take as mirror the rise and fall of former ages and learn from present success and failure" —

sentences.zh: 臣聞堯、舜之為君而天下之人理者，以其能任九官四嶽十二牧，不失其舉，不貳其業，不侵其職。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that Yao and Shun as rulers brought order to all under Heaven because they could appoint the nine ministers, the four mountain lords, and the twelve pasture lords — not missing the right appointment, not duplicating their tasks, not encroaching on their duties.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that Yao and Shun brought order to the realm because they could appoint the nine ministers, the four mountain lords, and the twelve pasture lords — making the right appointments, assigning clear duties, and never encroaching on their offices.

sentences.zh: 居官惟其能，左右惟其賢。

translations.literal: Those who held office were chosen for their ability; those at the ruler's side were chosen for their worth.
translations.idiomatic: Offices went to the capable; the ruler's circle to the worthy.

sentences.zh: 元凱在下，雖微必舉；

translations.literal: Yi Yin and Yu Ya were below, yet though humble they were surely raised up;
translations.idiomatic: Yi Yin and Yu Ya stood below, yet though humble they were surely elevated;

sentences.zh: 四凶在朝，雖強必誅。

translations.literal: The Four Evils were at court, yet though powerful they were surely executed.
translations.idiomatic: The Four Evils sat at court, yet though powerful they were surely punished.

sentences.zh: 考其安危，明其取捨。

translations.literal: Examine safety and danger; clarify what to take and what to discard.
translations.idiomatic: Weigh safety against danger; know what to embrace and what to reject.

sentences.zh: 至秦之二代，漢之元、成，咸欲措國如唐、虞，致身如堯、舜，而終敗亡者，以其不見安危之機，不知取捨之道，不任大臣，不辨姦人，不親忠良，不遠讒佞。

translations.literal: Down to the two generations of Qin and the Yuan and Cheng reigns of Han — all wished to set the state in order as in the age of Yao and Shun and to make themselves like Yao and Shun, yet in the end perished — because they did not see the pivot of safety and danger, did not know the way of choosing and discarding, did not entrust great ministers, did not distinguish wicked men, did not keep loyal worthies near, and did not keep slanderers and flatterers far.
translations.idiomatic: Down to the two generations of Qin and the Yuan and Cheng reigns of Han — all wished to govern like Yao and Shun, yet in the end perished because they failed to see the pivot of safety and danger, did not know what to embrace and reject, did not entrust great ministers, did not distinguish the wicked, did not keep loyal men near, and did not banish slanderers.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下察唐、虞之所以興，而景行於前；

translations.literal: Your subject humbly hopes Your Majesty will examine why Tang and Yu rose, and take that as a bright model ahead;
translations.idiomatic: I humbly urge Your Majesty to examine why Yao and Shun rose, and take that as your bright model;

sentences.zh: 鑒秦、漢之所以亡，而戒懼於後。

translations.literal: Take as mirror why Qin and Han perished, and be warned and fearful afterward.
translations.idiomatic: Take as mirror why Qin and Han fell, and be warned and vigilant hereafter.

sentences.zh: 陛下無謂廟堂無賢相，庶官無賢士。

translations.literal: Your Majesty must not say that in the temple hall there are no worthy chancellors and among the hundred offices there are no worthy scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Do not say that the court lacks worthy chancellors or that the offices lack worthy men.

sentences.zh: 今紀綱未絕，典刑猶在，人誰不欲致身為王臣，致時為太平，陛下何忽而不用之耶？

translations.literal: Now the statutes are not yet severed and the canonical punishments still remain — who would not wish to devote himself as a king's minister and bring his age to peace? Why does Your Majesty neglect them and not employ them?
translations.idiomatic: The statutes are not yet broken and the laws still stand — who would not wish to serve as your minister and bring peace to the age? Why does Your Majesty neglect them?

sentences.zh: 又有居官非其能，左右非其賢，其惡如四凶，其詐如趙高，其姦如恭、顯，陛下又何憚而不去之耶？

translations.literal: Moreover there are those who hold office beyond their ability and stand at the side though they are not worthy — wicked as the Four Evils, deceitful as Zhao Gao, treacherous as Gong Yu and Shi Xian — why should Your Majesty hesitate to remove them?
translations.idiomatic: And there are men in office beyond their ability and at your side though unworthy — wicked as the Four Evils, deceitful as Zhao Gao, treacherous as Gong Yu and Shi Xian — why should Your Majesty hesitate to remove them?

sentences.zh: 神器固有歸，天命固有分，祖廟固有靈，忠臣固有心，陛下其念之哉！

translations.literal: The sacred vessel has its proper destination; Heaven's mandate has its proper allotment; the ancestral temple has its numinous power; loyal ministers have their steadfast hearts — Your Majesty, reflect on this!
translations.idiomatic: The throne has its rightful holder; Heaven's mandate its proper allotment; the ancestral temple its numinous power; loyal ministers their steadfast hearts — Your Majesty, remember this!

sentences.zh: 昔秦之亡也，失於強暴；

translations.literal: In the past Qin's perishing lay in excessive harshness;
translations.idiomatic: Qin perished through excessive harshness;

sentences.zh: 漢之亡也，失於微弱。

translations.literal: Han's perishing lay in excessive weakness.
translations.idiomatic: Han perished through excessive weakness.

sentences.zh: 強暴則賊臣畏死而害上，微弱則姦臣竊權而震主。

translations.literal: When harsh, wicked ministers fear death and harm their ruler; when weak, treacherous ministers steal authority and shake their master.
translations.idiomatic: Harshness drives wicked ministers to kill their ruler from fear of death; weakness lets treacherous ministers steal power and intimidate the throne.

sentences.zh: 伏見敬宗皇帝不虞亡秦之禍，不翦其萌；

translations.literal: Your subject observes that Emperor Jingzong did not guard against the disaster of Qin's fall and did not cut off its first shoots;
translations.idiomatic: I observe that Emperor Jingzong did not guard against Qin's disaster and did not cut off its first shoots;

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下深軫亡漢之憂，以杜其漸。

translations.literal: Your subject humbly hopes Your Majesty will deeply feel the worry of Han's fall and stop its gradual growth.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly urge Your Majesty to deeply heed the lesson of Han's fall and stop the drift while it can still be stopped.

sentences.zh: 則祖宗之鴻業可紹，三五之遐軌可追矣。

translations.literal: Then the great enterprise of the ancestors may be continued and the distant tracks of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors may be pursued.
translations.idiomatic: Then the ancestors' great enterprise may be renewed and the distant example of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors may be pursued.

sentences.zh: 臣前所謂「陛下心有所未達，以下情塞而不能上通；

translations.literal: What your subject said earlier — "Your Majesty's mind has points it has not reached; below, feelings are blocked and cannot pass upward;
translations.idiomatic: What I said earlier — "Your Majesty's mind has not reached every truth; below, the people's feelings are blocked and cannot reach you;

sentences.zh: 行有所未孚，以上澤壅而不得下浹」者。

translations.literal: Your conduct has points it has not won trust; above, favor is dammed and cannot flow downward to soak all." —
translations.idiomatic: Your conduct has not won full trust; above, your grace is dammed and cannot reach the people below." —

sentences.zh: 且百姓塗炭之苦，陛下無由而知；

translations.literal: Moreover the people's suffering in fire and smearing — Your Majesty has no means to know it;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the people's suffering in misery — Your Majesty has no way to know it;

sentences.zh: 則陛下有子育之心，百姓無由而信。

translations.literal: Then though Your Majesty has the heart of nourishing children, the people have no means to believe it.
translations.idiomatic: Then though Your Majesty has a parent's heart for the people, they have no way to believe it.

sentences.zh: 臣謹按春秋書「梁亡」，不書取者，梁自亡也，以其思慮昏而耳目塞，上出惡政，人為寇盜，皆不知其所以然，以自取其滅亡也。

translations.literal: Your subject respectfully cites the Spring and Autumn Annals' record of "Liang perished," and does not record "was taken" — Liang destroyed itself, because its deliberations were muddled and its ears and eyes blocked; above it issued wicked government, and below men became bandits and robbers, yet none knew why — and so brought on its own destruction.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully cite the Spring and Autumn Annals' record of "Liang perished," and does not record "was taken" — Liang destroyed itself because its rulers' minds were clouded and their ears and eyes blocked; wicked policies issued from above, men became bandits below, and none knew why — and so brought ruin on themselves.

sentences.zh: 臣聞國君之所以尊者，重其社稷也；

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that the reason a state's ruler is honored is that he gives weight to his altars of soil and grain;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that a ruler is honored because he gives weight to the altars of state;

sentences.zh: 社稷之所以重者，存其百姓也。

translations.literal: The reason the altars of soil and grain are given weight is that the people are preserved.
translations.idiomatic: The altars are weighty because the people are preserved.

sentences.zh: 苟百姓之不存，則社稷不得固其重；

translations.literal: If the people are not preserved, then the altars cannot secure their weight;
translations.idiomatic: If the people are not preserved, the altars cannot hold their weight;

sentences.zh: 苟社稷之不重，則國君不得保其尊。

translations.literal: If the altars are not weighty, then the state's ruler cannot preserve his honor.
translations.idiomatic: If the altars lose their weight, the ruler cannot preserve his honor.

sentences.zh: 故治天下不可不知百姓之情。

translations.literal: Therefore in governing all under Heaven one cannot fail to know the people's condition.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore to govern the realm one must know the people's condition.

sentences.zh: 夫百姓者，陛下之赤子也。

translations.literal: The people are Your Majesty's red infants.
translations.idiomatic: The people are Your Majesty's own children.

sentences.zh: 陛下宜令仁慈者親育之，如保傅焉，如乳哺焉，如師之教導焉。

translations.literal: Your Majesty ought to have the benevolent personally nurture them — as protector and tutor, as nursing and feeding, as a teacher's instruction and guidance.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty ought to have the benevolent nurture them personally — as protector and tutor, as nurse and feeder, as teacher and guide.

sentences.zh: 故人信於上也，敬之如神明，愛之如父母。

translations.literal: Therefore when people trust their ruler above, they revere him as a spirit and love him as parents.
translations.idiomatic: When people trust their ruler, they revere him as a spirit and love him as a parent.

sentences.zh: 今或不然。

translations.literal: Now it is perhaps not so.
translations.idiomatic: Today it is not so.

sentences.zh: 陛下親近貴倖，分曹補署，建除卒吏，召致賔客，因其貨賄，假其氣勢。

translations.literal: Your Majesty keeps near the noble favorites; they are assigned by department and post; clerks of the Jian and Chu cycles are summoned and guests are brought in; relying on their bribes, you lend them your authority and momentum.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty keeps favored intimates near; they are assigned to offices by department; clerks and clients are summoned and installed; relying on their bribes, you lend them your authority.

sentences.zh: 大者統藩方，小者為牧守。

translations.literal: The greater ones command frontier regions; the lesser ones serve as prefects and governors.
translations.idiomatic: The greater ones command military regions; the lesser ones serve as prefects and governors.

sentences.zh: 居上無清惠之政。

translations.literal: In high office they have no pure and generous government.
translations.idiomatic: In high office they offer no pure and generous government.

sentences.zh: 而有饕餮之害；

translations.literal: Yet they have the harm of gluttonous devouring;
translations.idiomatic: Only the harm of gluttonous greed;

sentences.zh: 居下無忠誠之節，而有姦欺之罪。

translations.literal: In low office they have no loyal and steadfast integrity, but have the crime of treachery and deceit.
translations.idiomatic: In low office they show no loyal integrity, only treachery and fraud.

sentences.zh: 故人之於上也，畏之如豺狼，惡之如讎敵。

translations.literal: Therefore in their relation to their ruler above, people fear him as wolves and jackals and hate him as a sworn enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the people fear their rulers like wolves and jackals and hate them like sworn enemies.

sentences.zh: 今海內困窮，處處流散，饑者不得食，寒者不得衣，鰥寡孤獨者不得存，老幼疾病者不得養。

translations.literal: Now within the seas there is destitution and poverty; people are scattered everywhere; the hungry cannot obtain food, the cold cannot obtain clothing, widowers and orphans cannot survive, and the old, the young, and the sick cannot be cared for.
translations.idiomatic: Now the empire is destitute; people scatter everywhere; the hungry cannot eat, the cold cannot be clothed, widows and orphans cannot survive, and the old, young, and sick cannot be cared for.

sentences.zh: 加以國之權柄，專在左右，貪臣聚斂以固寵，姦吏因緣而弄法。

translations.literal: Added to this, the state's authority rests solely with those at the side; greedy ministers gather wealth to secure favor, and treacherous clerks exploit connections to manipulate the law.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the state's power rests solely with those at your side; greedy ministers extort wealth to secure favor, and corrupt clerks manipulate the law for their own ends.

sentences.zh: 冤痛之聲，上達于九天，下流於九泉，鬼神怨怒，陰陽為之愆錯。

translations.literal: The sounds of wrongful suffering reach up to the nine heavens and flow down to the nine springs; ghosts and spirits resent in anger, and yin and yang are thrown into disorder for it.
translations.idiomatic: Cries of injustice reach up to heaven and down to the underworld; ghosts and spirits seethe with anger, and yin and yang fall out of balance.

sentences.zh: 君門萬里而不得告訴，士人無所歸化，百姓無所歸命。

translations.literal: The ruler's gate is ten thousand li away and grievances cannot be told; scholars have nowhere to turn for guidance, and the people have nowhere to place their trust.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler's gate is ten thousand li away and grievances cannot be heard; scholars have nowhere to turn, and the people have nowhere to place their trust.

sentences.zh: 官亂人貧，盜賊並起，土崩之勢，憂在旦夕。

translations.literal: Officials are in disorder and the people are poor; bandits and robbers rise together; the momentum of earth collapsing — the worry lies within the day or the morrow.
translations.idiomatic: Officials are corrupt and the people impoverished; bandits rise on every side; the state is crumbling — disaster may come at any moment.

sentences.zh: 即不幸因之以疾癘，繼之以凶荒，臣恐陳勝、吳廣不獨起於秦，赤眉、黃巾不獨起於漢，故臣所以為陛下發憤扼腕，痛心泣血爾。

translations.literal: If misfortune adds plague upon this and famine and disaster follow, your subject fears that Chen Sheng and Wu Guang will not rise only in Qin, and the Red Eyebrows and Yellow Turbans will not rise only in Han — therefore your subject beats his breast and wrings his wrists for Your Majesty, his heart pained to the point of weeping blood.
translations.idiomatic: If plague and famine follow, I fear Chen Sheng and Wu Guang will rise again — not only in Qin — and the Red Eyebrows and Yellow Turbans — not only in Han. That is why I beat my breast in anguish and weep blood for Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 如此則百姓有塗炭之苦，陛下何由而知之；

translations.literal: If it is thus, then the people have suffering in fire and smearing — by what means can Your Majesty know it?
translations.idiomatic: If this is so, the people suffer in misery — how can Your Majesty know it?

sentences.zh: 陛下有子育之心，百姓安得而信之乎？

translations.literal: Your Majesty has the heart of nourishing children — how can the people believe it?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has a parent's heart for the people — how can they believe it?

sentences.zh: 致使陛下「行有所未孚，必有所未達」者，固其然也。

translations.literal: Causing Your Majesty's words — "Your conduct has points it has not won trust; there must be points your mind has not reached" — is naturally so.
translations.idiomatic: This is exactly what makes true your own words — "Your conduct has not won full trust; your mind has not reached every truth" — and no wonder.

sentences.zh: 臣聞昔漢元帝即位之初，更制七十餘事，其心甚誠，其稱甚美。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that at the beginning of Emperor Yuan of Han's accession, he changed more than seventy institutions; his heart was very sincere and his reputation very fine.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that when Emperor Yuan of Han first took the throne, he reformed more than seventy institutions; his heart was sincere and his reputation splendid.

sentences.zh: 然而紀綱日紊，國祚日衰，姦宄日強，黎元日困者，以其不能擇賢明而任之，失其操柄也。

translations.literal: Yet the statutes grew daily disordered, the dynastic fortune daily declined, wickedness daily strengthened, and the common people daily distressed — because he could not select the worthy and bright and employ them, and lost hold of the helm.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the statutes grew daily disordered, the dynasty daily declined, wickedness daily strengthened, and the people daily distressed — because he could not select worthy men and employ them, and lost hold of the helm.

sentences.zh: 即陛下御宇，憂勤兆庶，屢降德音，四海之內，莫不抗首而長思，自喜復生於死亡之中也。

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty holds the realm, you have toiled in worry and diligence for the myriad masses, repeatedly issuing virtuous pronouncements; within the four seas none failed to raise their heads and sigh long, rejoicing that they were reborn from among the dead.
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty has held the realm, you have toiled in worry and diligence for the myriad masses, repeatedly issuing virtuous pronouncements; throughout the four seas none failed to raise their heads and sigh with relief, rejoicing that they were reborn from among the dead.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下慎終如始，以塞萬方之望。

translations.literal: I prostrate myself and beg Your Majesty to be careful at the end as at the beginning, to satisfy the hopes of the ten thousand directions.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to be careful at the end as at the beginning, to satisfy the hopes of all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 誠能揭國權以歸其相，持兵柄以歸其將，去貪臣聚斂之政，除姦吏因緣之害，惟忠賢是近，惟正直是用，內寵便僻，無所聽焉。

translations.literal: If you can truly raise state authority and return it to the chancellor, hold the military handle and return it to the generals, remove the government of greedy ministers gathering levies, eliminate the harm of treacherous officials seizing opportunities, draw near only the loyal and worthy, employ only the upright — hear none of the words of inner favorites and convenient flatterers.
translations.idiomatic: If you can truly return state authority to the chancellor and military authority to the generals, remove the government of greedy ministers gathering levies, eliminate the harm of treacherous officials seizing opportunities, draw near only the loyal and worthy and employ only the upright — hear none of the words of inner favorites and convenient flatterers.

sentences.zh: 選清慎之官，擇仁惠之長，敏之以利，煦之以仁，教之以孝慈，導之以德義，去耳目之塞，通上下之情，俾萬國歡康，兆民蘇息，則心無不達，行無不孚矣。

translations.literal: Select officials who are clear and cautious, choose leaders who are benevolent and gracious, quicken them with benefit, warm them with benevolence, teach them with filial piety and kindness, guide them with virtue and righteousness, remove the blockage of ears and eyes, connect the feelings of above and below — then make the ten thousand states joyful and at peace, the myriad masses revive and rest; then what the heart intends will not fail to reach, what is enacted will not fail to win trust.
translations.idiomatic: Select officials who are clear and cautious, choose leaders who are benevolent and gracious, quicken them with benefit, warm them with benevolence, teach them filial piety and kindness, guide them with virtue and righteousness, remove the blockage of ears and eyes, connect the feelings of above and below — then make the ten thousand states joyful and at peace and the myriad masses revive and rest; then what you intend will reach everywhere and what you enact will win trust everywhere.

sentences.zh: 臣前所謂「欲兆人之化也，在脩己以先之」者。

translations.literal: What your subject earlier called "if you wish the myriad masses to be transformed, cultivate the self first to lead them" —
translations.idiomatic: What I said earlier — "if you wish the myriad masses to be transformed, cultivate yourself first to lead them" —

sentences.zh: 臣聞德以脩己，教以導人，脩之也則人不勸而自至，導之也則人敦行而率從。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard: virtue is for cultivating the self, teaching is for guiding others; cultivate it, then men without exhortation come of themselves; guide it, then men earnestly act and broadly follow.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard: virtue is for cultivating the self, teaching is for guiding others; cultivate it, then men without exhortation come of themselves; guide it, then men earnestly act and broadly follow.

sentences.zh: 是以君子欲政之必行也，故以身先之；

translations.literal: Therefore the noble man wishes government necessarily to be carried out, and so he takes the lead with his person;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the noble man wishes government to be carried out, and so he takes the lead with his own person;

sentences.zh: 欲人之從化也，故以道御之。

translations.literal: wishes men to follow transformation, and so he governs them with the Way.
translations.idiomatic: wishes men to follow transformation, and so he governs them with the Way.

sentences.zh: 今陛下先之以身而政未必行，御之以道而人未從化，豈不以立教之旨未盡其方也。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty takes the lead with your person yet government is not necessarily carried out, governs with the Way yet men have not followed transformation — is it that the aim of establishing teaching has not exhausted its methods?
translations.idiomatic: Now you take the lead with your person yet government is not necessarily carried out, govern with the Way yet men have not followed transformation — is it that the aim of establishing teaching has not exhausted its methods?

sentences.zh: 夫立教之方，在乎君以明制之，臣以忠行之，君以知人為明，臣以匡時為忠，知人則任賢而去邪，匡時則固本而守法。

translations.literal: The method of establishing teaching lies in the ruler clearly regulating it and the minister loyally carrying it out; the ruler takes knowing men as clarity, the minister takes correcting the times as loyalty; knowing men lies in employing the worthy and removing the perverse, correcting the times lies in securing the foundation and keeping to the law.
translations.idiomatic: The method of establishing teaching lies in the ruler clearly regulating it and the minister loyally carrying it out; the ruler takes knowing men as clarity, the minister takes correcting the times as loyalty; knowing men lies in employing the worthy and removing the perverse, correcting the times lies in securing the foundation and keeping to the law.

sentences.zh: 賢不任則重賞不足以勸善，邪不去則嚴刑不足以禁非，本不固則民流，法不守則政散，而欲教之使必至，化之使必行，不可得也。

translations.literal: If the worthy are not employed, heavy rewards are insufficient to encourage good; if the perverse are not removed, severe punishments are insufficient to prohibit wrong; if the foundation is not secure, people scatter; if the law is not kept, government disperses — yet wishing teaching necessarily to arrive and transformation necessarily to be carried out cannot be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: If the worthy are not employed, heavy rewards are insufficient to encourage good; if the perverse are not removed, severe punishments are insufficient to prohibit wrong; if the foundation is not secure, people scatter; if the law is not kept, government disperses — yet wishing teaching to arrive and transformation to be carried out cannot be obtained.

sentences.zh: 陛下能斥姦邪不私其左右，舉賢正不遺其疏遠，則化浹於朝廷矣；

translations.literal: If Your Majesty can repel treacherous perversity without favoring those at left and right, raise the worthy and upright without neglecting the distant — then transformation will soak the court;
translations.idiomatic: If you can repel treacherous perversity without favoring those at your side, raise the worthy and upright without neglecting the distant — then transformation will soak the court;

sentences.zh: 愛人以敦本，分職而奉法，脩其身以及其人，始於中而成於外，則化行於天下矣。

translations.literal: love others and enrich the foundation, divide duties and keep to the law, cultivate the self and extend to others, begin within and accomplish without — then transformation will travel all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: love others and enrich the foundation, divide duties and keep to the law, cultivate yourself and extend to others, begin within and accomplish without — then transformation will travel the realm.

sentences.zh: 臣前所謂「欲氣之和也，在於遂性以導之」者，當納人於仁壽也。

translations.literal: What your subject earlier called "if you wish the qi to be harmonious, follow their nature to guide them" — one should bring men into benevolence and longevity.
translations.idiomatic: What I said earlier — "if you wish the vital energies to harmonize, follow their nature to guide them" — one should bring the people into benevolence and longevity.

sentences.zh: 夫欲人之仁壽也，在乎立制度，脩教化。

translations.literal: If one wishes men benevolent and long-lived, it lies in establishing institutions and cultivating transformation.
translations.idiomatic: If one wishes the people benevolent and long-lived, it lies in establishing institutions and cultivating transformation.

sentences.zh: 夫制度立則財用省，財用省則賦斂輕，賦斂輕則人富矣；

translations.literal: When institutions are established, expenditures are economized; when expenditures are economized, levies are light; when levies are light, men are wealthy;
translations.idiomatic: When institutions are established, expenditures are economized; when expenditures are economized, levies are light; when levies are light, the people grow wealthy;

sentences.zh: 教化脩則爭競息，爭競息則刑罰清，刑罰清則人安矣。

translations.literal: when transformation is cultivated, contention ceases; when contention ceases, punishments are clear; when punishments are clear, men are at peace.
translations.idiomatic: when transformation is cultivated, contention ceases; when contention ceases, punishments are clear; when punishments are clear, the people are at peace.

sentences.zh: 旣富矣，則仁義興焉；

translations.literal: once wealthy, then benevolence and righteousness arise;
translations.idiomatic: once wealthy, then benevolence and righteousness arise;

sentences.zh: 旣安矣，則壽考至焉。

translations.literal: once at peace, then longevity arrives.
translations.idiomatic: once at peace, then longevity arrives.

sentences.zh: 仁壽之心感於下，和平之氣應於上，故災害不作，休祥荐臻，四方底寧，萬物咸遂矣。

translations.literal: Hearts of benevolence and longevity are moved below, qi of peace and harmony respond above — therefore disasters do not arise, auspicious omens arrive in succession, the four directions reach tranquility, and the ten thousand things all succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Hearts of benevolence and longevity are moved below, qi of peace and harmony respond above — therefore disasters do not arise, auspicious omens arrive in succession, the four directions reach tranquility, and the ten thousand things all succeed.

sentences.zh: 臣前所謂「救災旱在致乎精誠」者。

translations.literal: What your subject earlier called "relieving drought disaster lies in attaining utmost sincerity" —
translations.idiomatic: What I said earlier — "relieving drought and famine lies in attaining utmost sincerity" —

sentences.zh: 臣謹按春秋，魯僖公七月之中，三書不雨者，以其君有恤人之志也；

translations.literal: Your subject respectfully examines the Spring and Autumn Annals: within the seventh month of Duke Xi of Lu, thrice recording "no rain" — because that ruler had the purpose of caring for the people;
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully examine the Spring and Autumn Annals: within the seventh month of Duke Xi of Lu, "no rain" is recorded three times — because that ruler had a mind to care for the people;

sentences.zh: 魯文公三年之中，一書不雨者，以其君無憫人之心也。

translations.literal: within three years of Duke Wen, recording "no rain" once — because that ruler had no heart of compassion for the people.
translations.idiomatic: across three years of Duke Wen, it is recorded only once — because that ruler had no heart of compassion for the people.

sentences.zh: 故僖公致精誠而旱不害物，文公無卹憫而旱則成災。

translations.literal: Therefore when Xi attained sincerity, drought did not harm things; when Wen lacked care and compassion, drought became disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore when Xi attained sincerity, drought did not harm the crops; when Wen lacked care and compassion, drought became true disaster.

sentences.zh: 陛下誠能有卹人之心，則無成災之變矣。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty truly has a heart to care for the people, there will be no change that becomes disaster.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty truly has a heart to care for the people, there will be no change that becomes disaster.

sentences.zh: 臣前所謂「廣播植在視乎食力」者。

translations.literal: What your subject earlier called "broad sowing and planting depend on observing food strength" —
translations.idiomatic: What I said earlier — "broad sowing and planting depend on observing the people's capacity to produce food" —

sentences.zh: 臣謹按春秋：「君人者，必時視人之所勤。

translations.literal: Your subject respectfully examines the Spring and Autumn Annals: "One who rules the people must constantly observe what the people labor at.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully examine the Spring and Autumn Annals: "A ruler must constantly observe what the people labor at.

sentences.zh: 人勤於力，則功築罕；

translations.literal: When the people labor at strength, achievements and construction are rare;
translations.idiomatic: When the people labor at physical strength, public works grow scarce;

sentences.zh: 人勤於財，則貢賦少；

translations.literal: when they labor at wealth, tribute and levies are few;
translations.idiomatic: when they labor at wealth, tribute and levies shrink;

sentences.zh: 人勤於食，則百事廢。」

translations.literal: when they labor at food, the hundred affairs are abandoned."
translations.idiomatic: when they labor at securing food, the hundred affairs are abandoned."

sentences.zh: 今財食與人力皆勤矣，願陛下廢百事之勞，廣三時之務，則播植不愆矣。

translations.literal: Now wealth, food, and strength are all labored — your subject wishes Your Majesty to abandon the toil of the hundred affairs and broaden the duties of the three seasons, then sowing and planting will not fail.
translations.idiomatic: Today wealth, food, and strength are all overstrained. I beg Your Majesty to set aside the toil of the hundred affairs and broaden the work of the three farming seasons — then sowing and planting will not fail.

sentences.zh: 臣前所謂「國廩罕蓄，本乎冗食尚繁」者。

translations.literal: What your subject earlier called "the state's granaries hold little, because redundant consumption remains excessive" —
translations.idiomatic: What I said earlier — "the state's granaries hold little because redundant consumption remains excessive" —

sentences.zh: 臣謹按春秋「臧孫辰告糴于齊」，春秋譏其國無九年之蓄，一年不登而百姓饑。

translations.literal: Your subject respectfully examines the Spring and Autumn Annals: "Zangsun Chen requested grain from Qi." The Spring and Autumn Annals condemns him for lacking nine years' stores — one year of poor harvest and the hundred surnames hungered.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully examine the Spring and Autumn Annals: "Zangsun Chen requested grain from Qi." The Annals condemn him for lacking nine years' stores — one year of poor harvest and the common people went hungry.

sentences.zh: 臣願斥游惰之人以篤其耕植，省不急之費以贍其黎元，則廩蓄不乏矣。

translations.literal: Your subject wishes to expel idle wanderers to deepen farming and planting, economize non-urgent expenditures to nourish the black-headed masses, then granary stores will not run dry.
translations.idiomatic: I beg to expel idle wanderers to deepen farming, cut non-urgent expenditures to nourish the people — then granary stores will not run dry.

sentences.zh: 臣前所謂「吏道多端，本乎選用失當」者，由國家取人不盡其才，任人不明其要故也。

translations.literal: What your subject earlier called "the officials' Way is many-branched, rooted in selection and employment being inappropriate" — because the state does not take men's full talent, and employing men does not clarify the essentials.
translations.idiomatic: What I said earlier — "the officials' paths multiplying, rooted in wrongful selection and appointment" — this is because the state does not draw on men's full talents, and appointments do not clarify what truly matters.

sentences.zh: 今陛下之用人也，求其聲而不得其實；

translations.literal: Now in Your Majesty's employment of men, you seek their reputation but not their substance;
translations.idiomatic: Today in appointing men, Your Majesty seeks reputation but not substance;

sentences.zh: 故人之趨進也，務其末而不務其本。

translations.literal: therefore in men's rushing forward, they attend to the branches but not the root.
translations.idiomatic: therefore those who advance attend to show but not to substance.

sentences.zh: 臣願覈考課之實，定遷序之制，則多端之吏息矣。

translations.literal: Your subject wishes to examine and verify the substance of evaluations and fix the system of promotion and sequence, then the many-branched officials will cease.
translations.idiomatic: I beg to examine the substance of performance evaluations and fix the system of advancement — then the multiplied paths of officials will subside.

sentences.zh: 臣前所謂「豪猾踰檢，由中外之法殊」者，以其官禁不一也。

translations.literal: What your subject earlier called "overbearing and cunning men overstep bounds, because inner and outer laws differ" — because official prohibitions are not unified.
translations.idiomatic: What I said earlier — "the powerful and cunning overstepping bounds because inner and outer law differ" — because official prohibitions are not one.

sentences.zh: 臣謹按春秋，齊桓公盟諸侯不以日，而葵丘之盟特以日者，美其能宣明天子之禁，率奉王官之法，故春秋備而書之。

translations.literal: Your subject respectfully examines the Spring and Autumn Annals: when Duke Huan of Qi covenanted with the feudal lords, dates were not given; yet the covenant at Kuiqiu is specially dated — praising his ability to proclaim and clarify the Son of Heaven's prohibitions and lead in keeping to the royal officers' laws; therefore the Spring and Autumn Annals records it in full.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully examine the Spring and Autumn Annals: when Duke Huan of Qi covenanted with the feudal lords, dates were usually omitted; yet the covenant at Kuiqiu is specially dated — praising his ability to proclaim the Son of Heaven's prohibitions and lead the states in keeping to the royal laws; therefore the Annals record it in full.

sentences.zh: 夫官者，五帝、三王之所建也；

translations.literal: Offices were what the Five Emperors and Three Kings established;
translations.idiomatic: Offices were what the Five Emperors and Three Kings established;

sentences.zh: 法者，高祖、太宗之所制也。

translations.literal: laws were what Gaozu and Taizong enacted.
translations.idiomatic: laws were what Gaozu and Taizong enacted.

sentences.zh: 法宜畫一，官宜正名。

translations.literal: Laws should be drawn as one; offices should have corrected names.
translations.idiomatic: Laws should be unified; offices should have correct titles.

sentences.zh: 今又分外官、中官之員，立南司、北司之局，或犯禁於南，則亡命于北，或正刑于外，則破律於中，法出多門，人無所措，實由兵農勢異，而中外法殊也。

translations.literal: Now again outer officials and inner officials are divided in posts, Southern Bureau and Northern Bureau offices are established — if one violates prohibition in the south he flees to the north; if punished outside he breaks law within; laws issue from many gates and men have nowhere to set themselves — truly because military and agricultural power differ, and inner and outer laws are separate.
translations.idiomatic: Now again outer and inner officials are divided in posts, and Southern Bureau and Northern Bureau offices are established — violate a prohibition in the south and flee to the north; be punished outside and break the law within; laws issue from many gates and men have nowhere to turn — truly because military and agricultural power diverge, and inner and outer law are separate.

sentences.zh: 臣聞古者因井田而制軍賦，間農事以脩武備，提封約卒乘之數，命將在公卿之列，故兵農一致而文武同方，可以保乂邦家，式遏禍亂。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that in antiquity, through well-field land they regulated military levies, interspersed agricultural affairs to cultivate military readiness, took fiefs and reckoned chariot-and-foot numbers, and commanders were placed among dukes and ministers — therefore military and agriculture were one and civil and martial shared one direction, so as to secure and govern the state and family and check rebellious designs.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that in antiquity the well-field system regulated military levies, agricultural seasons were interwoven with military training, fiefs were tallied for chariot and foot numbers, and commanders were appointed from among the chief ministers — thus military and agriculture were one, civil and martial shared one direction, to secure the state and check rebellion.

sentences.zh: 暨太宗皇帝肇建邦典，亦置府兵，臺省軍衛，文武參掌，居閑歲則櫜弓力穡，將有事則釋耒荷戈，所以脩復古制，不廢舊物。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong first established the dynastic institutions, he also established fubing militia; Terrace offices and army guards, civil and martial jointly administered; in idle years they sheathed bows and exerted strength at sowing; when affairs arose they set aside plows and shouldered spears — thereby restoring the ancient system without abandoning the old institutions.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong first established the dynastic institutions, he also established the fubing militia; Terrace offices and army guards, civil and martial jointly administered; in peaceful years they sheathed bows and labored in the fields; when trouble arose they set aside plows and took up arms — thereby restoring the ancient system without abandoning the old institutions.

sentences.zh: 今則不然。

translations.literal: Now it is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Now it is not so.

sentences.zh: 夏官不知兵籍，止於奉朝請；

translations.literal: the Minister of War does not know military registers, stopping at attending court audience;
translations.idiomatic: the Minister of War does not know the military registers, and attends court only as a formality;

sentences.zh: 六軍不主兵事，止於養勳階。

translations.literal: the Six Armies do not preside over military affairs, stopping at nurturing ranks and merit.
translations.idiomatic: the Six Armies do not preside over military affairs, and exist only to nurture ranks and honors.

sentences.zh: 軍容合中官之政，戎律附內臣之職。

translations.literal: Military affairs merge with inner officials' government; military regulations attach to inner attendants' duties.
translations.idiomatic: Military affairs are merged with inner eunuch government; military regulations are attached to inner attendants' offices.

sentences.zh: 首一戴武弁，嫉文吏如仇讎；

translations.literal: One head dons the military cap and hates civil officials like sworn enemies;
translations.idiomatic: One head dons the military cap and hates civil officials like sworn enemies;

sentences.zh: 足一蹈軍門，視農夫如草芥。

translations.literal: one foot steps through the army gate and regards farmers like grass and husks.
translations.idiomatic: one foot steps through the army gate and regards farmers as nothing.

sentences.zh: 謀不足以翦除凶逆，而詐足以抑揚威福；

translations.literal: Their stratagems are insufficient to cut down treacherous rebels, yet their cunning suffices to raise and lower authority and favor;
translations.idiomatic: Their stratagems are insufficient to cut down treacherous rebels, yet their cunning suffices to raise and lower authority and favor;

sentences.zh: 勇不足以鎮衛社稷，而暴足以侵軼里閭。

translations.literal: their courage is insufficient to guard and secure the altars of soil and grain, yet their violence suffices to invade lanes and hamlets.
translations.idiomatic: their courage is insufficient to guard the altars of state, yet their violence suffices to prey on lanes and hamlets.

sentences.zh: 羈絏藩臣，干凌宰輔，隳裂王度，汨亂朝經。

translations.literal: They bind feudal ministers, overawe chief ministers, shatter the royal measure, and muddy and disorder court constants.
translations.idiomatic: They bind feudal ministers, overawe chief ministers, shatter the royal measure, and muddy the constants of court governance.

sentences.zh: 張武夫之威，上以制君父；

translations.literal: They display the might of warriors to control the ruler and father above;
translations.idiomatic: They display the might of warriors to control the ruler and father above;

sentences.zh: 假天子之命，下以御英豪。

translations.literal: they borrow the Son of Heaven's command to repel heroes below.
translations.idiomatic: they borrow the Son of Heaven's command to repel heroes below.

sentences.zh: 有藏姦觀釁之心，無伏節死難之義。

translations.literal: They have hearts that harbor treachery and watch for openings, but no principle of bowing to duty and dying in hardship.
translations.idiomatic: They harbor treachery and watch for openings, but have no principle of bowing to duty and dying in hardship.

sentences.zh: 豈先王經文緯武之旨耶！

translations.literal: Is this the purpose of the former kings in weaving civil and martial together!
translations.idiomatic: Is this the purpose of the former kings in weaving civil and martial together!

sentences.zh: 臣願陛下貫文武之道，均兵農之功，正貴賤之名，一中外之法，選軍衛之職，脩省署之官，近崇貞觀之規，遠復成周之制，自邦畿以刑于下國，始天子以達于諸侯，則可以制豪猾之強，無踰檢之患矣。

translations.literal: Your subject wishes Your Majesty to thread through civil and martial Ways, equalize military and agricultural achievements, correct names of noble and base, unify inner and outer laws, select army guards' duties, and repair provincial offices; near at hand honor the regulations of the Zhenguan reign, far off restore the institutions of the accomplished Zhou: from the capital domain discipline the subordinate states, beginning with the Son of Heaven and reaching the feudal lords — then one can restrain the strong among overbearing and cunning men, and there will be no calamity of overstepping bounds.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to thread civil and martial Ways together, equalize military and agricultural achievement, correct titles of noble and base, unify inner and outer law, select army guards' duties, and repair the provincial offices; near at hand honor the regulations of the Zhenguan reign, far off restore the institutions of the accomplished Zhou: from the capital domain discipline the subordinate states, from the Son of Heaven down to the feudal lords — then you can restrain the strong among overbearing and cunning men, and there will be no calamity of overstepping bounds.

sentences.zh: 臣前所謂「生徒墮業，由學校之官廢」者，蓋以國家貴其祿而賤其能，先其身而後其行，故庶官乏通經之學，諸生無脩業之心矣。

translations.literal: What your subject earlier called "students are idle in study, because school officials are abandoned" — broadly the state values their stipends and despises their ability, puts position before conduct; therefore the myriad offices lack learning that penetrates the classics, and the students have no heart to cultivate study.
translations.idiomatic: What I said earlier — "students growing idle because school offices are abandoned" — broadly the state values their stipends and despises their ability, puts position before conduct; therefore the myriad offices lack mastery of the classics, and students have no heart to cultivate their studies.

sentences.zh: 臣前所謂「列郡干禁，由授任非其人」者。

translations.literal: What your subject earlier called "the commanderies interfere with prohibitions, because appointment is to unfit men" —
translations.idiomatic: What I said earlier — "the commanderies interfering with prohibitions because the wrong men are appointed" —

sentences.zh: 臣以為刺史之任，理亂之根本繫焉，朝廷之法制在焉，權可以抑豪猾，恩可以惠孤寡，強可以禦姦寇，政可以移風俗。

translations.literal: Your subject holds that the duty of regional inspectors is where the root of order and disorder lies and where the court's laws and institutions reside; authority can repel overbearing strongmen, kindness can benefit orphans and widows, strength can repel treacherous bandits, and government can shift customs and mores.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that the post of regional inspector is where the root of order and disorder lies and where the court's laws and institutions reside; with authority one can repel overbearing strongmen, with kindness benefit orphans and widows, with strength repel treacherous bandits, and with government shift customs and mores.

sentences.zh: 其將校有曾經戰陣，及功臣子弟，各請隨宜酬賞。

translations.literal: As for commanders and officers who have passed through battle lines, and sons and younger brothers of meritorious ministers — each asks to be rewarded according to fitness.
translations.idiomatic: As for commanders and officers who have seen battle, and the sons and younger brothers of meritorious ministers — each asks to be rewarded as appropriate.

sentences.zh: 如無治人之術者，不當授任此官，則絕干禁之患矣。

translations.literal: If one lacks the art of governing men, he should not hold this office — then the calamity of interfering with prohibitions will be ended.
translations.idiomatic: If one lacks the art of governing men, he should not hold this office — then the calamity of interfering with prohibitions will end.

sentences.zh: 臣前所謂「百工淫巧，由制度不立」者。

translations.literal: What your subject earlier called "the hundred crafts are excessive in cleverness, because institutions are not established" —
translations.idiomatic: What I said earlier — "the hundred crafts growing excessive in cleverness because institutions are not established" —

sentences.zh: 臣請以官位祿秩，制其器用車服，禁人金銀珠玉錦繡雕鏤不蓄於私室，則無蕩心之巧矣。

translations.literal: Your subject asks to regulate implements, vehicles, and dress by office rank and stipend grade, and prohibit gold, silver, pearls, jade, brocade, embroidery, and carving and inlay from being stored in private chambers — then there will be no cleverness that unsettles the heart.
translations.idiomatic: I ask to regulate implements, vehicles, and dress by office rank and stipend grade, and prohibit gold, silver, pearls, jade, brocade, embroidery, and carving and inlay from being hoarded in private chambers — then there will be no cleverness that unsettles the heart.

sentences.zh: 臣前所謂「辨枝葉」者，考其言以詢行也。

translations.literal: What your subject earlier called "distinguishing branches and leaves" — examining words inquires into conduct.
translations.idiomatic: What I said earlier — "distinguishing branches and leaves" — this is because examining words inquires into conduct.

sentences.zh: 臣前所謂「形于耻格」者，導德而齊禮也。

translations.literal: What your subject earlier called "taking form in shame and regulation" — guiding through virtue and aligning ritual.
translations.idiomatic: What I said earlier — "taking form in shame and regulation" — this is because guiding through virtue aligns ritual.

sentences.zh: 臣前所謂「念生寡而食衆，可罷斥惰遊」者，已備之於前矣。

translations.literal: What your subject earlier called "reflecting that producers are few and consumers many — idle wanderers may be dismissed" — has already been set forth above.
translations.idiomatic: What I said earlier — "reflecting that producers are few and consumers many, and that idle wanderers may be dismissed" — has already been set forth above.

sentences.zh: 臣前所謂「令煩而理鮮，要察其行否」者。

translations.literal: What your subject earlier called "orders are numerous yet governance is rare — the essential is to examine whether they are carried out" —
translations.idiomatic: What I said earlier — "orders being numerous yet governance rare, and that the essential is to examine whether they are carried out" —

sentences.zh: 臣聞號令者，乃理國之具也，君審而出之，臣奉而行之，或虧上旨，罪在不赦。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that commands are the instruments of governing the state: the ruler examines and issues them, ministers receive and carry them out — to violate the superior intent is a crime not pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that commands are the instruments of governing the state: the ruler examines and issues them, ministers receive and carry them out — to violate the superior intent is an unpardonable crime.

sentences.zh: 今陛下令煩而理鮮，得非持之者有所蔽欺乎？

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty's orders are numerous yet governance is rare — can it be that those who hold them have something they conceal and deceive?
translations.idiomatic: Today Your Majesty's orders are numerous yet governance is rare — can it be that those who hold them conceal and deceive?

sentences.zh: 臣前所謂「博延群彥，願陛下必納其言；

translations.literal: What your subject earlier said — "broadly extend to gather worthy men, and your subject wishes Your Majesty will surely accept their words;
translations.idiomatic: What I said earlier — "broadly gather worthy men, and I beg Your Majesty to accept their words;

sentences.zh: 造廷待問，則小臣不敢愛死」者。

translations.literal: come to court and await inquiry — then would this petty official dare cherish his life" —
translations.idiomatic: come to court and await inquiry — then would this petty official dare cherish his life" —

sentences.zh: 臣聞晁錯為漢畫削諸侯之策，非不知禍之將至也。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that Chao Cuo for Han drew up the plan to reduce the feudal lords — it was not that he did not know disaster was about to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that Chao Cuo drew up the plan to reduce the feudal lords for Han — it was not that he did not know disaster was coming.

sentences.zh: 忠臣之心，壯夫之節，苟利社稷，死無悔焉。

translations.literal: The loyal minister's heart, the stalwart's integrity: if it profits the altars of soil and grain, death brings no regret.
translations.idiomatic: The loyal minister's heart, the stalwart's integrity: if it profits the altars of state, death brings no regret.

sentences.zh: 今臣非不知言發而禍應，計行而身戮，蓋所以痛社稷之危，哀生人之困，豈忍姑息時忌，竊陛下一命之寵哉！

translations.literal: Now your subject is not unaware that when words issue disaster responds, when plans are carried out the body is punished — broadly grieving the altars' peril and mourning the living people's distress: how could he bear to temporize with the times' taboos and steal one life of Your Majesty's favor!
translations.idiomatic: Now I am not unaware that when words issue disaster follows, and when plans are carried out the body is punished — I grieve the altars' peril and mourn the people's suffering: how could I bear to temporize with the times' taboos and steal one life of Your Majesty's favor!

sentences.zh: 昔龍逢死而啟殷，比干死而啟周，韓非死而啟漢，陳蕃死而啟魏。

translations.literal: Formerly Long Feng died and Shang was awakened; Bi Gan died and Zhou was awakened; Han Fei died and Han was awakened; Chen Fan died and Wei was awakened.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Long Feng died and Shang was awakened; Bi Gan died and Zhou was awakened; Han Fei died and Han was awakened; Chen Fan died and Wei was awakened.

sentences.zh: 今臣之來也，有司或不敢薦臣之言，陛下又無以察臣之心，退必受戮於權臣之手。

translations.literal: Now in your subject's coming, the responsible offices perhaps dare not recommend your subject's words; Your Majesty again has no means to discern your subject's heart — on retiring he will surely be executed at the hands of powerful ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Now in my coming, the responsible offices perhaps dare not recommend my words; Your Majesty again has no means to discern my heart — on retiring I will surely be executed at the hands of powerful ministers.

sentences.zh: 臣幸得從四子於地下，固臣之願也。

translations.literal: Your subject would be fortunate to follow the Four in the underworld — that is indeed your subject's wish.
translations.idiomatic: I would be fortunate to follow the Four in the underworld — that is indeed my wish.

sentences.zh: 所不知殺臣者，臣死之後，將孰為啟之哉？

translations.literal: What is unknown is: when your subject is killed, after your subject's death, who will awaken them?
translations.idiomatic: What I do not know is: when I am killed, after my death, who will awaken them?

sentences.zh: 至於人主之闕，政教之疵，前日之弊，臣旣言之矣。

translations.literal: As for the ruler's faults, the flaws in government and teaching, and the abuses of former days — your subject has already spoken of them.
translations.idiomatic: As for the ruler's faults, the flaws in government and teaching, and the abuses of former days — I have already spoken of them.

sentences.zh: 若乃流下土之惠，修近古之理，而致其和平者，在陛下行之而已。

translations.literal: As for spreading benefit to the lower lands, cultivating governance like that of near antiquity, and attaining peace — it lies in Your Majesty's carrying it out, nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: As for spreading benefit to the lower lands, cultivating governance like that of near antiquity, and attaining peace — it lies in Your Majesty's carrying it out, nothing more.

sentences.zh: 然上之所陳者，實以臣親奉聖問，敢不條對。

translations.literal: Yet what was set forth above was truly because your subject personally received the sage inquiry — how dare he not respond item by item.
translations.idiomatic: Yet what was set forth above was truly because I personally received the sage inquiry — how could I not respond item by item.

sentences.zh: 雖臣之愚，以為未極教化之大端，皇王之要道。

translations.literal: Though your subject is foolish, he holds that it has not reached the great beginning of transformation and teaching, the essential Way of the august kings.
translations.idiomatic: Though I am foolish, I hold that it has not reached the great beginning of transformation and teaching, the essential Way of the august kings.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下事天地以教人敬，奉宗廟以教人孝，養高年以教人悌長，字百姓以教人慈幼，調元氣以煦育，扇大和於仁壽，可以逍遙無為，垂拱成化。

translations.literal: I prostrate myself: may Your Majesty serve Heaven and Earth to teach men reverence, attend the ancestral temples to teach men filial piety, nurture the aged to teach men brotherly respect for elders, cherish the hundred surnames to teach men kindness to the young, harmonize the primordial qi to warm and nurture, fan the great harmony to benevolence and longevity — then you can roam free in non-action, fold your arms and let transformation be accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to serve Heaven and Earth to teach reverence, attend the ancestral temples to teach filial piety, nurture the aged to teach respect for elders, cherish the people to teach kindness to the young, harmonize the vital energies to warm and nurture, fan the great harmony toward benevolence and longevity — then you may roam free in non-action, fold your arms, and let transformation be accomplished.

sentences.zh: 至若念陶鈞之道，在擇宰相而任之，使權造物之柄；

translations.literal: As for reflecting on the potter's wheel — it lies in selecting chief ministers to entrust with it, letting them wield the handle of creation and transformation;
translations.idiomatic: As for reflecting on the potter's wheel — it lies in selecting chief ministers to entrust with it, letting them wield the handle of creation and transformation;

sentences.zh: 念保定之功，在擇將帥而任之，使修分閫之寄；

translations.literal: reflecting on securing and stabilizing achievement — it lies in selecting generals and commanders to entrust with it, letting them fulfill the trust outside the frontier passes;
translations.idiomatic: reflecting on securing and stabilizing the realm — it lies in selecting generals and commanders to entrust with it, letting them fulfill the trust outside the frontier passes;

sentences.zh: 念百度之未貞，在擇庶官而任之，使專職業之守；

translations.literal: reflecting on the hundred measures' lack of correctness — it lies in selecting the myriad offices to entrust with it, letting them focus on keeping to their professional duties;
translations.idiomatic: reflecting on the hundred measures' lack of correctness — it lies in selecting the myriad offices to entrust with it, letting them focus on keeping to their professional duties;

sentences.zh: 念百姓之愁痛，在擇長吏而任之，使明惠育之術。

translations.literal: reflecting on the hundred surnames' grievance and pain — it lies in selecting good local officials to entrust with it, letting them clarify the arts of kindness and nurturing.
translations.idiomatic: reflecting on the people's grievance and pain — it lies in selecting good local officials to entrust with it, letting them clarify the arts of kindness and nurturing.

sentences.zh: 自然言足以為天下教，行足以為天下法，仁足以勸善，義足以禁非，又何必宵衣旰食，勞神惕慮，然後以致其理哉！

translations.literal: Then naturally words suffice to be the realm's teaching, conduct suffices to be the realm's model, benevolence suffices to encourage good, righteousness suffices to prohibit wrong — why must one rise at midnight and dine at dusk, toil the spirit and be vigilant in thought, only then attain governance!
translations.idiomatic: Then naturally your words suffice to teach the realm, your conduct suffices to model it, your benevolence suffices to encourage good, your righteousness suffices to prohibit wrong — why must you rise at midnight and dine at dusk, toil your spirit and be ever vigilant, only then attain governance!

sentences.zh: 是歲，左散騎常侍馮宿、太常少卿賈餗、庫部郎中龎嚴為考策官，三人者，時之文士也，覩蕡條對，歎服嗟悒，以為漢之晁、董無以過之。

translations.literal: That year, Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry Feng Su, Vice Minister of Rites Jia Su, and Bureau Director of the Storehouses Pang Yan served as examination graders for the policy essays; the three were literary men of the time. Seeing Fen's itemized answers, they sighed in admiration and lamentation, holding them to surpass the ancient Chao and Dong.
translations.idiomatic: That year Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry Feng Su, Vice Minister of Rites Jia Su, and Bureau Director of the Storehouses Pang Yan served as examination graders for the policy essays; the three were literary men of the time. Seeing Liu Fen's itemized answers, they sighed in admiration and lamentation, holding them to surpass the ancient Chao Cuo and Dong Zhongshu.

sentences.zh: 言論激切，士林感動。

translations.literal: The discourse was incisive and impassioned, and the scholar community was deeply moved.
translations.idiomatic: The discourse was incisive and impassioned, and the scholar community was deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 時登科者二十二人，而中官當途，考官不敢留蕡在籍中，物論喧然不平之。

translations.literal: At the time twenty-two passed the examination, but inner eunuchs held power and the examiners dared not keep Fen on the roster; public opinion clamored in outrage.
translations.idiomatic: At the time twenty-two passed the examination, but inner eunuchs held power and the examiners dared not keep Liu Fen on the roster; public opinion clamored in outrage.

sentences.zh: 守道正人，傳讀其文，至有相對埀泣者。

translations.literal: Upright men who kept to the Way circulated his text, and some wept face to face as they read it.
translations.idiomatic: Upright men who kept to the Way circulated his text, and some wept face to face as they read it.

sentences.zh: 諌官御史，扼腕憤發，而執政之臣，從而弭之，以避黄門之怨。

translations.literal: Remonstrating officials and investigating censors clenched their wrists in indignation, but the ministers in power smoothed matters over to avoid the yellow gate's resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrating officials and investigating censors clenched their wrists in indignation, but the ministers in power smoothed matters over to avoid the yellow gate's resentment.

sentences.zh: 唯登科人李邰謂人曰：「劉蕡不第，我軰登科，實厚顔矣。」

translations.literal: Only Li He, who had passed the examination, said to others: "Liu Fen did not place, yet our cohort passed — how thick is our face indeed."
translations.idiomatic: Only Li He, who had passed the examination, said to others: "Liu Fen did not place, yet our cohort passed — how thick is our face indeed."

sentences.zh: 請以所授官讓蕡，事雖不行，人士多之。

translations.literal: He asked to yield the office he had received to Fen; though the matter was not granted, scholars praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to yield the office he had received to Fen; though the matter was not granted, scholars praised him.

sentences.zh: 令狐楚在興元，牛僧孺鎮襄陽，辟為從事，待如師友。

translations.literal: Linghu Chu was at Xingyuan and Niu Sengru was stationed at Xiangyang; each recruited Fen as a staff member and treated him like a teacher or friend.
translations.idiomatic: Linghu Chu was at Xingyuan and Niu Sengru was stationed at Xiangyang; each recruited Liu Fen as a staff member and treated him like a teacher or friend.

sentences.zh: 位終使府御史。

translations.literal: He ended his career as censor on a military commissioner's staff.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as censor on a military commissioner's staff.

sentences.zh: 李商隱，字義山，懷州河內人。

translations.literal: Li Shangyin, style name Yishan, was a man of Henei in Huai prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shangyin, whose courtesy name was Yishan, came from Henei in Huai prefecture.

sentences.zh: 曾祖叔恒，年十九登進士第，位終安陽令。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Shuhuan passed the jinshi at nineteen and ended as magistrate of Anyang.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Shuhuan passed the jinshi examination at nineteen and ended his career as magistrate of Anyang.

sentences.zh: 祖俌，位終邢州錄事參軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Fu ended as recording secretary of Xing prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Fu rose no higher than recording secretary of Xing prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父嗣。

translations.literal: His father was Si.
translations.idiomatic: His father was Si.

sentences.zh: 商隱幼能為文。

translations.literal: Shangyin could compose essays while still young.
translations.idiomatic: Shangyin could already write essays as a boy.

sentences.zh: 令狐楚鎮河陽，以所業文干之，年才及弱冠。

translations.literal: When Linghu Chu was military commissioner of Heyang, Shangyin presented his writings to him; he had not yet reached twenty.
