translations.idiomatic: When Linghu Chu governed Heyang as military commissioner, Shangyin presented his writings to him, though he had not yet turned twenty.

sentences.zh: 楚以其少俊，深禮之，令與諸子遊。

translations.literal: Chu regarded him as young and talented, treated him with deep courtesy, and had him associate with his sons.
translations.idiomatic: Chu admired his youth and talent, treated him with exceptional courtesy, and let him mingle with his sons.

sentences.zh: 楚鎮天平、汴州，從為巡官，歲給資裝，令隨計上都。

translations.literal: When Chu governed Tianping and Bian prefectures, Shangyin followed him as a staff officer; Chu supplied his travel expenses yearly and sent him to the capital with the tribute mission for the examination.
translations.idiomatic: When Chu served at Tianping and Bian, Shangyin followed him as a staff officer. Chu paid his travel expenses each year and sent him to the capital with the tribute mission to sit for the examination.

sentences.zh: 開成二年，方登進士第，釋褐秘書省校書郎，調補弘農尉。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaicheng he finally passed the jinshi, was first appointed proofreader in the Secretariat, and was later transferred to magistrate of Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: In 837 he finally passed the jinshi examination, took his first office as proofreader in the Secretariat, and was later transferred to magistrate of Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 會昌二年，又以書判拔萃。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huichang he again passed the examination for outstanding legal and documentary skill.
translations.idiomatic: In 842 he again distinguished himself in the examination for legal and documentary excellence.

sentences.zh: 王茂元鎮河陽，辟為掌書記，得待御史。

translations.literal: When Wang Maoyuan was commissioner of Heyang, he recruited Shangyin as chief clerk and obtained for him the post of awaiting imperial disposition as censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Maoyuan governed Heyang, he recruited Shangyin as chief clerk and secured for him appointment as censor awaiting imperial disposition.

sentences.zh: 茂元愛其才，以子妻之。

translations.literal: Maoyuan admired his talent and gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Maoyuan admired his talent and gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 茂元雖讀書為儒，然本將家子，李德裕素遇之，時德裕秉政，用為河陽帥。

translations.literal: Although Maoyuan had studied and was a Confucian scholar, he was by origin from a military family; Li Deyu had long favored him, and at the time Deyu held power and appointed him commander of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Maoyuan had studied the classics and was a Confucian in learning, yet he came from a military family. Li Deyu had long favored him, and while Deyu held power he appointed him commander of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 德裕與李宗閔、楊嗣復、令狐楚大相仇怨。

translations.literal: Deyu bore great enmity toward Li Zongmin, Yang Sifu, and Linghu Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu was locked in bitter enmity with Li Zongmin, Yang Sifu, and Linghu Chu.

sentences.zh: 商隱既為茂元從事，宗閔黨大薄之。

translations.literal: Since Shangyin had entered Maoyuan's service, Zongmin's faction looked down on him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shangyin entered Maoyuan's service, Zongmin's faction held him in deep contempt.

sentences.zh: 時令狐楚已卒，子綯為員外郎，以商隱背恩，尤惡其無行。

translations.literal: By then Linghu Chu had died; his son Tao was an outer court official. Regarding Shangyin as ungrateful, he especially detested his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: By then Linghu Chu had died and his son Tao held an outer court post. Tao regarded Shangyin as ungrateful and especially despised his lack of principle.

sentences.zh: 俄而茂元卒，來遊京師，久之不調。

translations.literal: Before long Maoyuan died; Shangyin came to the capital seeking office but went long without appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Maoyuan died. Shangyin came to the capital in search of office but remained unemployed for a long time.

sentences.zh: 會給事中鄭亞廉察桂州，請為觀察判官、檢校水部員外郎。

translations.literal: Presently Supervising Secretary Zheng Ya was commissioned to inspect Guizhou; he invited Shangyin as administrative aide of the observation commission and acting vice director of the Ministry of Waterways.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Supervising Secretary Zheng Ya was sent to inspect Guizhou. He invited Shangyin to serve as administrative aide on the observation staff and acting vice director of the Ministry of Waterways.

sentences.zh: 大中初，白敏中執政，令狐綯在內署，共排李德裕逐之。

translations.literal: In the early Dazhong era Bai Minzhong held power; Linghu Tao was in the inner secretariat; together they drove out Li Deyu.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dazhong reign Bai Minzhong came to power, with Linghu Tao in the inner secretariat; together they forced Li Deyu from office.

sentences.zh: 亞坐德裕黨，亦貶循州刺史。

translations.literal: Ya was implicated as a member of Deyu's faction and was also demoted to prefect of Xunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ya was condemned as a member of Deyu's faction and was demoted to prefect of Xunzhou.

sentences.zh: 商隱隨亞在嶺表累載。

translations.literal: Shangyin followed Ya in the Lingnan region for several years.
translations.idiomatic: Shangyin followed Ya in the far south for several years.

sentences.zh: 三年入朝，京兆尹盧弘正奏署掾曹，令典箋奏。

translations.literal: After three years he entered court; the capital intendant Lu Hongzheng memorialized to appoint him to his staff and had him oversee petitions and memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he returned to court. The capital intendant Lu Hongzheng memorialized to place him on his staff and put him in charge of petitions and memorials.

sentences.zh: 明年，令狐綯作相，商隱屢啟陳情，綯不之省。

translations.literal: The next year Linghu Tao became chief minister; Shangyin repeatedly submitted petitions explaining his situation, but Tao paid no attention.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Linghu Tao became chief minister. Shangyin repeatedly petitioned to explain his circumstances, but Tao ignored him.

sentences.zh: 弘正鎮徐州，又從為掌書記。

translations.literal: When Hongzheng was commissioner at Xuzhou, Shangyin again followed him as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Hongzheng governed Xuzhou, Shangyin again served him as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 府罷入朝，復以文章干襜，乃補太學博士。

translations.literal: When the office expired he returned to court; he again sought advancement through his writings and was appointed Erudite of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: When that appointment ended he returned to court, again pressed his literary writings in search of office, and was appointed Erudite of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 會河南尹柳仲郢鎮東蜀，辟為節度判官、檢校工部郎中。

translations.literal: Presently the Henan intendant Liu Zhongying was commissioned to the eastern Shu region; he recruited Shangyin as military commissioner's administrative aide and acting director of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Henan intendant Liu Zhongying was sent to govern the eastern Shu region. He recruited Shangyin as administrative aide on his staff and acting director of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 大中末，仲郢坐專殺左遷，商隱廢罷，還鄭州，未幾病卒。

translations.literal: In the late Dazhong period Zhongying was demoted for unauthorized execution; Shangyin was dismissed, returned to Zhengzhou, and soon after died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Dazhong reign Zhongying was demoted for an unauthorized execution. Shangyin was dismissed, returned to Zhengzhou, and died of illness not long afterward.

sentences.zh: 商隱能為古文，不喜偶對。

translations.literal: Shangyin could write in the ancient style and disliked parallel couplets.
translations.idiomatic: Shangyin could write in the ancient prose style and disliked regulated parallel composition.

sentences.zh: 從事令狐楚幕。

translations.literal: He served on Linghu Chu's staff.
translations.idiomatic: He had served on Linghu Chu's staff.

sentences.zh: 楚能章奏，遂以其道授商隱，自是始為今體章奏。

translations.literal: Chu was skilled at memorials and decrees and thus transmitted this art to Shangyin; from then on he began writing modern-style memorials and decrees.
translations.idiomatic: Chu excelled at memorials and edicts and taught Shangyin that craft, after which Shangyin began to write in the contemporary style of court documents.

sentences.zh: 博學強記，下筆不能自休，尤善為誄奠之辭。

translations.literal: Broad in learning and strong in memory, he could not stop once he set pen to paper, and was especially adept at dirges and offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Learned and with a formidable memory, he wrote tirelessly once he took up the brush and was especially skilled at dirges and funeral offerings.

sentences.zh: 與太原溫庭筠、南郡段成式齊名，時號“三十六”。

translations.literal: He was famed alongside Wen Tingyun of Taiyuan and Duan Chengshi of Nancheng; at the time they were called the Thirty-six.
translations.idiomatic: His fame stood with Wen Tingyun of Taiyuan and Duan Chengshi of Nancheng; contemporaries called them the "Thirty-six."

sentences.zh: 文思清麗，庭筠過之。

translations.literal: His literary thought was clear and beautiful; he surpassed Tingyun.
translations.idiomatic: His literary sensibility was clear and refined, and in this he surpassed Tingyun.

sentences.zh: 而俱無持操，恃才詭激，為當涂者所薄。

translations.literal: Yet both lacked moral constancy; relying on talent they were eccentric and incendiary, and those in power despised them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet both lacked firm moral principle. They relied on talent, behaved with eccentric vehemence, and men in power looked down on them.

sentences.zh: 名宦不進，坎壈終身。

translations.literal: They did not advance in official fame and were frustrated throughout life.
translations.idiomatic: Neither advanced in official career and both were thwarted to the end of their lives.

sentences.zh: 弟羲叟，亦以進士擢第，累為賔佐。

translations.literal: His younger brother Yishou also passed the jinshi and served repeatedly as a staff member.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Yishou also passed the jinshi examination and served repeatedly on provincial staffs.

sentences.zh: 商隱有表狀集四十卷。

translations.literal: Shangyin had a collection of memorials and petitions in forty juan.
translations.idiomatic: Shangyin left a collection of memorials and formal petitions in forty juan.

sentences.zh: 温庭筠者，太原人，本名岐，字飛卿。

translations.literal: Wen Tingyun was a man of Taiyuan; his original name was Qi, style name Feiqing.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Tingyun came from Taiyuan. His original name was Qi, and his courtesy name was Feiqing.

sentences.zh: 大中初應進士，苦心硯席，尤長於詩賦。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Dazhong era he took the jinshi examination, toiled at inkstone and mat, and was especially skilled in poetry and fu.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Dazhong reign he sat for the jinshi examination, labored over his studies, and excelled above all in poetry and rhapsodies.

sentences.zh: 初至京師，人士翕然推重，然士行塵雜，不脩邉幅，能逐絃吹之音為側艶之詞。

translations.literal: When he first reached the capital, scholars and officials all at once esteemed him; yet his conduct was dusty and mixed, he did not keep his appearance in order, and could follow string and wind music to compose sensuous lyrics.
translations.idiomatic: When he first arrived in the capital, men of letters immediately held him in high regard. Yet his personal conduct was disorderly, he paid no heed to decorum, and he could set sensuous lyrics to the music of strings and pipes.

sentences.zh: 公卿家無賴子弟裴誠、令狐滈之徒，相與蒱飲酣醉終日，由是累年不第。

translations.literal: With the worthless sons of high officials such as Pei Cheng and Linghu Hao, they gambled and drank together, drunk all day, and for this reason he failed the examination year after year.
translations.idiomatic: He consorted with the dissolute sons of great families, such as Pei Cheng and Linghu Hao, gambling and drinking with them in drunken revelry all day long. Because of this he failed the examination year after year.

sentences.zh: 徐商鎮襄陽，往依之，署為巡官。

translations.literal: When Xu Shang governed Xiangyang, Tingyun went to rely on him and was appointed touring officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Shang was stationed at Xiangyang, Tingyun went to join his staff and was appointed a touring officer.

sentences.zh: 咸通中，失意歸江東，路由廣陵，心怨令狐綯在位時不為成名。

translations.literal: In the Xiantong era, disheartened, he returned to the lands east of the Yangzi; passing through Guangling, he resented that Linghu Tao while in power had not helped him achieve fame.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiantong reign, disheartened, he returned to the lower Yangzi region. Passing through Guangling, he nursed resentment that Linghu Tao, while in office, had not helped him win renown.

sentences.zh: 既至，與新進少年狂遊狹邪，乆不刺謁，又乞索於楊子院，醉而犯夜，為虞候所撃，敗面折齒方還。

translations.literal: Once there, he roamed the pleasure quarters wildly with newly risen young men, long neglected to pay calls, and also begged at Yangzi Courtyard; drunk he violated the night curfew, was beaten by the night watch, and returned only after his face was ruined and teeth broken.
translations.idiomatic: Once there, he caroused wildly in the pleasure quarters with young upstarts, long neglected formal calls on officials, and even begged at Yangzi Courtyard. Drunk, he broke the night curfew, was beaten by the night watch, and returned with his face battered and teeth broken.

sentences.zh: 揚州訴之，令狐綯捕虞候治之，極言庭筠狹邪醜迹，乃兩釋之。

translations.literal: Yangzhou brought suit; Linghu Tao arrested the night watch and prosecuted him, speaking at length of Tingyun's disreputable conduct in the pleasure quarters, and then released both.
translations.idiomatic: The Yangzhou authorities brought suit. Linghu Tao had the night watch arrested and prosecuted, speaking at length of Tingyun's disreputable conduct in the pleasure quarters, and then released both parties.

sentences.zh: 自是汙行聞于京師。

translations.literal: From then on his disgraceful conduct became known in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: From then on his disreputable conduct became known throughout the capital.

sentences.zh: 庭筠自至長安，致書公卿間雪寃，屬徐商知政事，頗為言之。

translations.literal: Tingyun, having reached Chang'an, sent letters among the high officials to clear his name; as Xu Shang was then directing state affairs, he spoke on his behalf at some length.
translations.idiomatic: After reaching Chang'an, Tingyun wrote to high officials to clear his name. Xu Shang was then directing state affairs and spoke on his behalf with some effect.

sentences.zh: 無何，商罷相，出鎮楊，收怒之，貶為方城尉，再遷隋縣尉，卒。

translations.literal: Before long Shang was removed as chief minister and went out to govern Yang; Shou grew angry with Tingyun, demoted him to magistrate of Fangcheng, later transferred him to magistrate of Sui county, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Xu Shang was dismissed as chief minister and took up a post at Yangzhou. Shou grew angry with Tingyun, demoted him to magistrate of Fangcheng, later transferred him to magistrate of Sui county, where he died.

sentences.zh: 子憲，以進士擢第。

translations.literal: His son Xian passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xian passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 弟庭皓，咸通中為徐州從事。

translations.literal: His younger brother Tinghao, in the Xiantong era, served as staff officer at Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Tinghao served on the staff at Xuzhou during the Xiantong reign.

sentences.zh: 節度使崔彦魯為龎勛所殺，庭皓亦被害。

translations.literal: The military governor Cui Yanlu was killed by Pang Xun, and Tinghao was also killed.
translations.idiomatic: When the military governor Cui Yanlu was killed by Pang Xun, Tinghao was killed as well.

sentences.zh: 庭筠著述頗多，而詩賦韻格清㧞，文士稱之。

translations.literal: Tingyun's writings were quite numerous, and the tonal pattern of his poetry and fu was clear and refined; men of letters praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Tingyun wrote a great deal, and the tonal craft of his poetry and rhapsodies was clear and refined. Men of letters praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 薛逢，字陶臣，河東人。

translations.literal: Xue Feng, style name Taochen, was a man of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Feng, whose courtesy name was Taochen, came from Hedong.

sentences.zh: 父倚。

translations.literal: His father was Yi.
translations.idiomatic: His father was Yi.

sentences.zh: 逢㑹昌初進士，擢第釋褐，祕書省校書郎崔罷相鎮河中，辟為從事。

translations.literal: Feng passed the jinshi at the beginning of the Huichang era, received appointment and left common dress; when Cui, proofreader at the Secretariat, was dismissed as chief minister and governed Hedzhong, he recruited Feng as staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: Feng passed the jinshi at the start of the Huichang reign, received office, and entered service. When Cui, a proofreader in the Secretariat, was dismissed as chief minister and took up command at Hedzhong, he recruited Feng to his staff.

sentences.zh: 鉉復輔政，奏授萬年尉，直文舘，累遷侍御史尚書郎。

translations.literal: When Xuan again assisted in government, he memorialized to appoint Feng wannian magistrate and assign him to the Hall of Literature; he was promoted repeatedly to supervising censor and a director in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuan again took up chief ministerial duties, he memorialized to appoint Feng magistrate of Wannian and assign him to the Hall of Literature. Feng was later promoted repeatedly to supervising censor and then to a director in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 逢文詞俊㧞，論議激切，自負經畫之畧，乆之不逹。

translations.literal: Feng's literary language was brilliant and refined, his discourse sharp and impassioned; he prided himself on strategic planning, yet for long he did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Feng's writing was brilliant and his discourse sharp and impassioned. He prided himself on strategic talent, yet for years he failed to advance.

sentences.zh: 應進士時，與彭城劉瑑尤相善，而瑑詞藝不迨逢，逢每侮之。

translations.literal: When taking the jinshi examination, he was especially close to Liu Cuan of Pengcheng, but Cuan's literary skill did not match Feng's, and Feng often belittled him.
translations.idiomatic: While sitting for the jinshi examination he was especially close to Liu Cuan of Pengcheng. Cuan's literary skill did not match Feng's, and Feng often treated him with contempt.

sentences.zh: 至大中末，瑑揚，歴禁署，逢愈不得意，自是相怨。

translations.literal: By the end of Dazhong Cuan rose in fame, passed through the inner offices, and Feng grew all the more discontent; from then on they resented each other.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of the Dazhong reign Cuan had risen to fame and served in the inner offices, while Feng grew ever more frustrated. From then on the two bore each other resentment.

sentences.zh: 俄而瑑知政事，或薦逢知制誥，瑑奏曰：「先朝立制兩省，官給事中舍人，除拜湏先歴州縣，逢未甞治郡，宜先試之。」

translations.literal: Before long Cuan directed state affairs; someone recommended Feng for drafting edicts, and Cuan memorialized, saying: 'The former court established the rule for the Two Departments that officials of drafting review and secretariat must first serve in prefectures and counties. Feng has never governed a commandery and should first be tried in such a post.'
translations.idiomatic: Before long Cuan took charge of state affairs. Someone recommended Feng for the post of drafter of edicts, but Cuan memorialized: "The former court established that appointees to the drafting and secretariat posts of the Two Departments must first serve in prefectural and county office. Feng has never governed a commandery and should first be tested in such a post."

sentences.zh: 乃出為巴州刺史。

translations.literal: Feng was then sent out as prefect of Bazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Feng was then sent out as prefect of Bazhou.

sentences.zh: 既而沈詢、楊收、王鐸由學士相繼為将相，皆同年進士，而逢文藝最優。

translations.literal: Before long Shen Xun, Yang Shou, and Wang Duo, rising from academicians, succeeded one another as chief ministers and generals; all were jinshi of the same year, yet Feng's literary art was the finest.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Shen Xun, Yang Shou, and Wang Duo rose from the Hanlin Academy to become chief ministers and generals in succession. All were jinshi of the same year as Feng, yet his literary talent was the finest.

sentences.zh: 楊収作相，後逢有詩云：「湏知金印朝天客。

translations.literal: When Yang Shou became chief minister, Feng later had a poem saying: "One must know the guest bearing the golden seal who faces the court.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang Shou became chief minister, Feng wrote a poem that ran: "One must know the courtier bearing the golden seal who faces the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 同是沙隄避路人。

translations.literal: Both alike are passers-by avoiding the road on the sand embankment.
translations.idiomatic: Both alike are passers-by sidestepping the road along the sand embankment.

sentences.zh: 威鳯偶時皆瑞聖，濳龍無水謾通神。」

translations.literal: A majestic phoenix appearing at the right moment is an auspicious sage; a hidden dragon without water vainly communicates with the divine."
translations.idiomatic: A majestic phoenix appearing at the right moment is hailed as an auspicious sage; a hidden dragon without water vainly claims communion with the divine."

sentences.zh: 收聞，大衘之。

translations.literal: When Shou heard of it, he was greatly resentful.
translations.idiomatic: When Shou heard of it, he was deeply offended.

sentences.zh: 又出為蓬州刺史。

translations.literal: Feng was again sent out as prefect of Pengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Feng was again sent out as prefect of Pengzhou.

sentences.zh: 收罷相，入為太常少卿給事中。

translations.literal: When Shou was removed as chief minister, Feng entered court as vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and drafting reviewer.
translations.idiomatic: When Shou was dismissed as chief minister, Feng entered court as vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and drafting reviewer.

sentences.zh: 王鐸作相，逢又有詩云：「昨日鴻毛萬鈞重，今朝山嶽一塵輕鐸。」

translations.literal: When Wang Duo became chief minister, Feng again had a poem saying: 'Yesterday a goose feather weighed ten thousand jun; today mountains and peaks are lighter than a speck of dust Duo.'
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Duo became chief minister, Feng wrote another poem: "Yesterday a goose feather weighed ten thousand jun; today mountains and peaks are lighter than a speck of dust."

sentences.zh: 又怨之，以恃才褊忿，人士鄙之。

translations.literal: Duo again resented him; because Feng relied on talent and was narrow and resentful, men of standing despised him.
translations.idiomatic: Duo again resented him. Because Feng relied on his talent and was narrow and quick to take offense, men of standing despised him.

sentences.zh: 遷祕書監，卒。

translations.literal: He was transferred to director of the Secretariat and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director of the Secretariat and died.

sentences.zh: 子廷珪，中和中，登進士第。

translations.literal: His son Tinggui, in the Zhonghe era, passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tinggui passed the jinshi examination during the Zhonghe reign.

sentences.zh: 大順初，累遷司勲員外郎，知制誥正，拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Datong he was promoted repeatedly to vice director in the Ministry of Honors, then formally appointed drafter of edicts, and invested as secretariat drafter.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Datong reign he rose through several posts to vice director in the Ministry of Honors, was formally appointed drafter of edicts, and was invested as secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 乾寧三年，奉使太原，復命昭宗幸華州，改左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qianning he was sent on mission to Taiyuan; on reporting back that Emperor Zhaozong was visiting Huazhou, he was changed to left regular attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In 896 he was sent on mission to Taiyuan. On reporting back that Emperor Zhaozong had moved to Huazhou, he was appointed left regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 移疾，免客遊成都。

translations.literal: He pleaded illness, was dismissed from office, and traveled as a guest in Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded illness, resigned from office, and traveled as a guest in Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 光化中，復為中書舍人，遷刑部吏部二侍郎，權知禮部貢舉，拜尚書左丞。

translations.literal: In the Guanghua era he again became secretariat drafter, was transferred to vice ministers of Justice and Personnel, acted as director of the Ministry of Rites examination, and was invested as left vice director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: During the Guanghua reign he again became secretariat drafter, was promoted to vice minister of both Justice and Personnel, served as acting director of the civil examinations in the Ministry of Rites, and was appointed left vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 入梁，至禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Entering Liang, he reached minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: After entering the service of Later Liang, he rose to minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 李拯，字昌時，隴西人。

translations.literal: Li Zheng, style name Changshi, was a man of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zheng, whose courtesy name was Changshi, came from Longxi.

sentences.zh: 咸通十二年登進士第。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Xiantong he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In 871 he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 乾符中，累佐府幕。

translations.literal: In the Qianfu era he repeatedly served on provincial staffs.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianfu reign he served repeatedly on provincial staffs.

sentences.zh: 黄巢之亂，避地平陽。

translations.literal: During Huang Chao's rebellion he fled to Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: During Huang Chao's rebellion he took refuge at Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 僖宗還京，召拜尚書郎，轉考功郎中、知制誥。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xizong returned to the capital, Zheng was summoned and appointed a director in the Secretariat, then transferred to director in the Ministry of Honors and made drafter of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xizong returned to the capital, Zheng was summoned and appointed a director in the Secretariat, then promoted to director in the Ministry of Honors and made drafter of edicts.

sentences.zh: 僖宗再幸寳鷄，拯扈從不及。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xizong again visited Baoji, Zheng could not keep up in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xizong again moved to Baoji, Zheng was unable to accompany him.

sentences.zh: 在鳯翔，襄王僭號，逼為翰林學士，拯既汚偽署，心不自安。

translations.literal: At Fengxiang the Prince of Xiang usurped a title; Zheng was forced to become Hanlin academician. Having been stained by a false appointment, his heart was not at ease.
translations.idiomatic: At Fengxiang the Prince of Xiang usurped an imperial title and forced Zheng to serve as a Hanlin academician. Having been tainted by service under the usurping regime, he could not rest easy in his mind.

sentences.zh: 後朱玫秉政，百揆無叙，典章濁亂。

translations.literal: Later Zhu Mei held power; the hundred officials were without order and institutions were turbid and chaotic.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhu Mei seized power. The hundred officials fell into disorder, and court institutions sank into chaos.

sentences.zh: 拯甞朝退，駐馬國門，望南山而吟曰：「紫宸朝罷綴鴛鸞，丹鳯樓前駐馬看。

translations.literal: Zheng once, after court was dismissed, halted his horse at the Gate of the Nation, gazed at the southern mountains and recited: "After court at Zichen ends, paired mandarin ducks are strung together; before the Crimson Phoenix Tower I halt my horse to look.
translations.idiomatic: Once, after court was dismissed, Zheng halted his horse at the Gate of the Nation, gazed toward the southern mountains, and recited: "After court at Zichen ends, paired mandarin ducks are strung together; before the Crimson Phoenix Tower I halt my horse to look.

sentences.zh: 唯有終南山色在，晴明依舊滿長安。」

translations.literal: Only the color of Mount Zhongnan remains; clear and bright as ever, filling Chang'an."
translations.idiomatic: Only the color of Mount Zhongnan remains, clear and bright as ever, filling Chang'an."

sentences.zh: 吟已涕下。

translations.literal: When he finished reciting, tears fell.
translations.idiomatic: When he finished reciting, tears streamed down his face.

sentences.zh: 及王行瑜殺朱玫，襄王出奔。

translations.literal: When Wang Xingyu killed Zhu Mei, the Prince of Xiang fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Xingyu killed Zhu Mei, the Prince of Xiang fled.

sentences.zh: 京城亂，拯為亂兵所殺。

translations.literal: The capital fell into chaos, and Zheng was killed by mutinous troops.
translations.idiomatic: The capital fell into chaos, and Zheng was killed by mutinous troops.

sentences.zh: 妻盧氏知書能文有姿色，拯既死，伏其屍慟哭，賊逼之，堅哭不動。

translations.literal: His wife, née Lu, was learned, could write, and was beautiful in appearance. After Zheng died she lay over his corpse wailing; when bandits pressed her, she continued weeping and did not move.
translations.idiomatic: His wife, Lady Lu, was learned, could write, and was beautiful. After Zheng died she lay over his corpse wailing. When bandits pressed her, she kept weeping and would not move.

sentences.zh: 又臨之以兵，至於斷一臂，終不顧，為賊所害，人皆傷之。

translations.literal: They again threatened her with weapons, even severing one arm, yet she never looked back and was killed by the bandits; all mourned her.
translations.idiomatic: They threatened her with weapons and even severed one of her arms, yet she never turned away and was killed by the bandits. All who heard of it mourned her.

sentences.zh: 李巨川，字下已，隴右人。

translations.literal: Li Juchuan, style name Xiayi, was a man of Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Juchuan, whose courtesy name was Xiayi, came from Longyou.

sentences.zh: 國初十八學士道玄之後，故相逢吉之姪曽孫。

translations.literal: A descendant of Li Daoxuan of the founding eighteen scholars, he was thus the grandnephew of Li Fengji.
translations.idiomatic: He was a descendant of Li Daoxuan of the founding eighteen scholars and a grandnephew of Li Fengji.

sentences.zh: 父循，大中八年登進士第。

translations.literal: His father Xun passed the jinshi in the eighth year of Dazhong.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xun passed the jinshi examination in 854.

sentences.zh: 巨川乾符中應進士，屬天下大亂，流離奔播，切於禄位，乃以刀筆從諸侯府。

translations.literal: Juchuan took the jinshi in the Qianfu era; as the realm fell into great disorder and he wandered in exile, eager for salary and rank, he relied on the pen and joined the staffs of regional lords.
translations.idiomatic: Juchuan sat for the jinshi during the Qianfu reign. As the realm fell into great disorder and he wandered in exile, eager for salary and rank, he turned to the pen and entered the staffs of regional lords.

sentences.zh: 王重榮鎮河中，辟為掌書記。

translations.literal: When Wang Chongrong governed Hedzhong, he recruited Juchuan as chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Chongrong was stationed at Hedzhong, he recruited Juchuan as chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 時車駕在蜀，賊據京師，重榮匡合諸藩，叶力誅冦，軍書奏請，堆案盈几。

translations.literal: At that time the imperial carriage was in Shu, bandits held the capital, and Chongrong united the regional lords and joined forces to suppress the rebels; military dispatches and memorials piled on desks until they overflowed.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor was in Shu, rebels held the capital, and Chongrong rallied the regional lords to join forces against the bandits. Military dispatches and memorials piled on his desk until they overflowed.

sentences.zh: 巨川文思敏速，翰動如飛，傳之藩隣，無不聳動，重榮收復功，巨川之助也。

translations.literal: Juchuan's literary thought was swift and sharp, his brush moved like flight; when transmitted to neighboring regions none failed to be stirred. Chongrong's merit in recovery was Juchuan's assistance.
translations.idiomatic: Juchuan wrote with swift brilliance, his brush flying across the page. When his dispatches reached neighboring regions, all were stirred. Chongrong's success in recovery owed much to Juchuan's help.

sentences.zh: 及重榮為部下所害，朝議罪叅佐，貶為漢中掾。

translations.literal: When Chongrong was killed by his subordinates, court opinion blamed his staff and Juchuan was demoted to aide in Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongrong was killed by his subordinates, court opinion blamed his staff, and Juchuan was demoted to an aide in Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 時楊守亮帥興元，素知之聞巨川至，喜謂客曰：“天以李書記遺我也！”

translations.literal: At that time Yang Shouliang commanded Xingyuan, knew him of old, and when he heard Juchuan had arrived said joyfully to a guest: 'Heaven has bequeathed Secretary Li to me!'
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yang Shouliang commanded Xingyuan and knew Juchuan of old. When he heard Juchuan had arrived, he said joyfully to a guest: "Heaven has sent Secretary Li to me!"

sentences.zh: 即命管記室，累遷幕職。

translations.literal: [Close quotation.] He immediately appointed him to manage the secretariat and promoted him through staff posts.
translations.idiomatic: [Close quotation.] He immediately appointed Juchuan to manage the secretariat and promoted him through several staff posts.

sentences.zh: 景福中，守亮為李茂貞所攻，城䧟，以部下數百人欲投太原。

translations.literal: In the Jingfu era Shouliang was attacked by Li Maozhen; the city fell, and with several hundred followers he wished to go over to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingfu reign Shouliang was attacked by Li Maozhen. When the city fell, he set out with several hundred followers intending to go over to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 入秦，為華軍所擒。

translations.literal: Entering Qin, he was captured by the Hua army.
translations.idiomatic: Entering Qin, he was captured by Han Jian's army at Hua.

sentences.zh: 巨川時從守亮，亦被械繫。

translations.literal: Juchuan was then following Shouliang and was also shackled.
translations.idiomatic: Juchuan was then with Shouliang and was shackled as well.

sentences.zh: 在途，巨川題詩於樹葉以遺華帥韓建，詞情哀鳴，建欣然解縛。

translations.literal: On the road Juchuan inscribed a poem on a tree leaf and sent it to Han Jian, commander of Hua; the language was mournful and plaintive, and Jian gladly released his bonds.
translations.idiomatic: On the road Juchuan inscribed a poem on a tree leaf and sent it to Han Jian, commander of Hua. The verse was mournful and moving, and Jian gladly released him from his bonds.

sentences.zh: 守亮誅，即命為掌書記。

translations.literal: When Shouliang was executed, Jian immediately appointed Juchuan chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: After Shouliang was executed, Jian immediately appointed Juchuan chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 俄而李茂貞犯京師，天子駐蹕於華。

translations.literal: Before long Li Maozhen invaded the capital, and the Son of Heaven halted at Hua.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Li Maozhen invaded the capital, and the emperor halted at Hua.

sentences.zh: 韓建以一州之力，供億萬乘，慮其不濟，遣巨川傳檄天下，請助轉餉，同匡王室，完葺京城。

translations.literal: Han Jian, with the strength of one province, supplied the myriad equipage of the imperial host and feared it would not suffice; he sent Juchuan to circulate a proclamation throughout the realm asking aid in transporting provisions, jointly to restore the royal house and repair the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Han Jian, with the resources of a single province, had to supply the imperial court and feared he could not manage it. He sent Juchuan to circulate a proclamation throughout the realm requesting aid in transporting provisions, so that all might jointly restore the royal house and rebuild the capital.

sentences.zh: 四方書檄，酬報輻湊，巨川灑翰陳敘，文理俱愜，昭宗深重之，即時巨川之名聞于天下。

translations.literal: Dispatches and replies from the four directions converged in streams; Juchuan wielded the brush and set forth accounts, his language and reasoning both satisfying. Emperor Zhaozong held him in deep esteem, and at once Juchuan's name was known throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Dispatches and replies poured in from every direction. Juchuan drafted responses with fluent prose and satisfying logic. Emperor Zhaozong held him in deep esteem, and Juchuan's name at once spread throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 昭宗還京，特授諌議大夫，仍留佐建。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhaozong returned to the capital, Juchuan was specially appointed remonstrance grandee and remained to assist Jian.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhaozong returned to the capital, Juchuan was specially appointed remonstrance grandee and remained to assist Han Jian.

sentences.zh: 光化初，朱全忠䧟河中，進兵入潼關。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guanghua Zhu Quanzhong captured Hedzhong and advanced into Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Guanghua reign Zhu Quanzhong captured Hedzhong and advanced into Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 建懼，令巨川見全忠送欵，至河中，從容言事。

translations.literal: Jian was afraid and had Juchuan go to see Quanzhong to offer submission; arriving at Hedzhong, he spoke of affairs at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was afraid and sent Juchuan to see Zhu Quanzhong and offer submission. Arriving at Hedzhong, Juchuan spoke calmly of the situation.

sentences.zh: 巨川指陳利害，全忠方圖問鼎，聞巨川所陳，心惡之。

translations.literal: Juchuan pointed out advantages and harms; Quanzhong was then plotting to seize the throne, and when he heard what Juchuan set forth his heart hated it.
translations.idiomatic: Juchuan laid out the advantages and dangers of the situation. Zhu Quanzhong was then plotting to seize the throne, and when he heard Juchuan's analysis he took offense.

sentences.zh: 判官敬翔，亦以文筆見知於全忠，慮得巨川減落名價，謂全忠曰“李諌議文章信美，但不利主人。”

translations.literal: The aide Jing Xiang, also known to Quanzhong for his literary skill, feared that gaining Juchuan would diminish his own fame and said to Quanzhong: 'Remonstrance Grandee Li's writing is indeed fine, but it does not benefit his master.'
translations.idiomatic: The aide Jing Xiang, also valued by Zhu Quanzhong for his literary skill, feared that keeping Juchuan would diminish his own standing and said to Quanzhong: "Remonstrance Grandee Li's writing is indeed fine, but it does not serve his master well."

sentences.zh: 是日為全忠所害。

translations.literal: [Close quotation.] That same day he was killed by Quanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: [Close quotation.] That same day Juchuan was killed by Zhu Quanzhong.

sentences.zh: 司空圖，字表聖，本臨淄人。

translations.literal: Sikong Tu, style name Biaosheng, was originally a man of Linzi.
translations.idiomatic: Sikong Tu, whose courtesy name was Biaosheng, was originally from Linzi.

sentences.zh: 曽祖遂，密令。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Sui was magistrate of Mi.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Sui served as magistrate of Mi.

sentences.zh: 祖彖，水部郎中。

translations.literal: His grandfather Luan was director in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Luan served as director in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 父輿，精吏術。

translations.literal: His father Yu was skilled in administrative methods.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yu was skilled in administrative methods.

sentences.zh: 大中初，戸部侍郎盧弘正領鹽鐵，奏輿為安邑兩池榷鹽使、檢校司封郎中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dazhong Vice Minister of Revenue Lu Hongzheng oversaw salt and iron and memorialized to appoint Yu commissioner of the Anyi two-pool salt monopoly and acting director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Dazhong reign Vice Minister of Revenue Lu Hongzheng oversaw the salt and iron monopoly and memorialized to appoint Yu commissioner of the Anyi two-pool salt monopoly and acting director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 先是，鹽法條例疎闊，吏多犯禁；

translations.literal: Previously the salt laws and regulations were loose and broad, and officials often violated prohibitions;
translations.idiomatic: Previously the salt laws were loosely defined, and officials often violated the regulations;

sentences.zh: 輿乃特定新法十條奏之，至今以為便。

translations.literal: Yu then specially fixed ten articles of new law and memorialized them; to this day they are regarded as convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Yu then drafted ten articles of new regulations and memorialized them. To this day they are regarded as convenient.

sentences.zh: 入朝為司門員外郎，遷戸部郎中，卒。

translations.literal: Entering court he became vice director in the Ministry of Justice, was transferred to director in the Ministry of Revenue, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court service as vice director in the Ministry of Justice, was promoted to director in the Ministry of Revenue, and died.

sentences.zh: 圖咸通十年登進士第，主司王凝於進士中尤奇之。

translations.literal: Tu passed the jinshi in the tenth year of Xiantong; the chief examiner Wang Ning regarded him as especially remarkable among the jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: Tu passed the jinshi examination in 869. The chief examiner Wang Ning regarded him as especially remarkable among the successful candidates.

sentences.zh: 凝左授商州刺史，圖請從之，凝加器重，洎廉問宣歙，辟為上客。

translations.literal: When Ning was demoted and appointed prefect of Shangzhou, Tu asked to follow him; Ning valued him all the more, and when he inspected Xuancheng and Shezhou he recruited Tu as chief guest.
translations.idiomatic: When Ning was demoted to prefect of Shangzhou, Tu asked to accompany him. Ning valued him all the more, and when Ning was assigned to inspect Xuancheng and Shezhou he recruited Tu as chief guest.

sentences.zh: 召拜殿中侍御史，以赴闕遲留，責授光祿寺主簿，分司東都。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed palace censor; because he was late in arriving at court he was demoted to registrar in the Court of Imperial Entertainments and assigned to the eastern capital branch.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed palace censor. Because he was slow in reaching court he was demoted to registrar in the Court of Imperial Entertainments and assigned to the eastern capital branch.

sentences.zh: 乾符六年，宰相盧攜罷免，以賔客分司，圖與之遊，攜嘉其高節，厚禮之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Qianfu Chief Minister Lu Xie was dismissed and served as guest at the eastern capital branch; Tu associated with him, Xie admired his lofty integrity, and treated him with generous courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: In 879 Chief Minister Lu Xie was dismissed and served as a guest at the eastern capital branch. Tu kept company with him. Xie admired Tu's lofty integrity and treated him with generous courtesy.

sentences.zh: 嘗過圖舍，手題于壁曰：「姓氏司空貴，官班御史卑，老夫如且在，不用念屯奇。」

translations.literal: Once visiting Tu's house, he wrote by hand on the wall: 'The surname Sikong is noble; the official rank of censor is low. If this old man were still in place, you need not brood over hardship and strangeness.'
translations.idiomatic: Once, visiting Tu's house, he wrote on the wall by hand: "The surname Sikong is noble; the rank of censor is low. If this old man were still in office, you need not brood over hardship and obscurity."

sentences.zh: 明年，攜復入朝，路由陝虢，謂陝帥盧渥曰：「司空御史，高士也，公其厚之。」

translations.literal: The next year Xie again entered court; passing through Shanzhou and Guozhou he said to the Shan commander Lu Wo: 'Censor Sikong is a lofty man; you should treat him generously.'
translations.idiomatic: The next year Xie returned to court. Passing through Shanzhou and Guozhou he said to the Shan commander Lu Wo: "Censor Sikong is a man of lofty character. You should treat him generously."

sentences.zh: 渥即日奏為賔佐。

translations.literal: Wo that same day memorialized to appoint him staff member.
translations.idiomatic: Wo that same day memorialized to appoint Tu to his staff.

sentences.zh: 其年，攜復知政事，召圖為禮部員外郎，賜緋魚袋，遷本司郎中。

translations.literal: That year Xie again directed state affairs, summoned Tu as vice director in the Ministry of Rites, granted him the crimson robe and fish bag, and transferred him to director in that ministry.
translations.idiomatic: That year Xie again took charge of state affairs, summoned Tu as vice director in the Ministry of Rites, granted him the crimson robe and fish bag, and promoted him to director in that ministry.

sentences.zh: 其年冬，巢賊犯京師，天子出幸，圖從之不及，乃退還河中。

translations.literal: That winter Huang Chao's bandits invaded the capital; the Son of Heaven went on tour, Tu could not keep up, and withdrew to Hedzhong.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Huang Chao's rebels invaded the capital. The emperor fled, Tu was unable to accompany him, and withdrew to Hedzhong.

sentences.zh: 時故相王徽亦在蒲，待圖頗厚。

translations.literal: At that time the former chief minister Wang Hui was also at Pu and treated Tu quite generously.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the former chief minister Wang Hui was also at Pu and treated Tu with great generosity.

sentences.zh: 數年，徽受詔鎮潞，乃表圖為副使，徽不赴鎮而止。

translations.literal: Several years later Hui received orders to govern Lu and memorialized to appoint Tu deputy commissioner; Hui did not go to his post and the matter ended.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later Hui received orders to take command at Lu and memorialized to appoint Tu his deputy. Hui never took up the post, and the appointment came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 僖宗自蜀還，次鳳翔，召圖知制誥，尋正拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xizong returned from Shu and halted at Fengxiang, Tu was summoned to draft edicts and soon formally appointed secretariat drafter.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xizong returned from Shu and halted at Fengxiang, Tu was summoned to draft edicts and soon formally appointed secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 其年僖宗出幸寶雞，復從之不及，退還河中。

translations.literal: That year Emperor Xizong went on tour to Baoji; Tu again could not keep up and withdrew to Hedzhong.
translations.idiomatic: That year Emperor Xizong moved to Baoji. Tu again could not accompany him and withdrew to Hedzhong.

sentences.zh: 龍紀初，復召拜舍人，未幾又以疾辭。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longji he was again summoned and appointed drafter; before long he again pleaded illness and resigned.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Longji reign he was again summoned and appointed secretariat drafter. Before long he again pleaded illness and resigned.

sentences.zh: 河北亂，乃寓居華陰。

translations.literal: When Hebei fell into disorder, he took up residence at Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: When Hebei fell into disorder, he took up residence at Huayin.

sentences.zh: 景福中，又以諫議大夫徵。

translations.literal: In the Jingfu era he was again summoned as remonstrance grandee.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingfu reign he was again summoned as remonstrance grandee.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷微弱，紀綱大壞，圖自深惟出不如處，移疾不起。

translations.literal: At that time the court was weak and institutions greatly ruined; Tu deeply reflected that going out was not as good as staying put, pleaded illness, and did not rise.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the court was weak and institutions were in ruins. Tu deeply felt that leaving retirement was worse than remaining in seclusion, pleaded illness, and refused to take office.

sentences.zh: 乾寧中，又以戶部侍郎徵，一至闕廷致謝，數日乞還山，許之。

translations.literal: In the Qianning era he was again summoned as vice minister of revenue; he once reached the court to offer thanks, and within days begged to return to the mountains and was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianning reign he was again summoned as vice minister of revenue. He came once to court to offer thanks, but within days begged to return to the mountains and was permitted to do so.

sentences.zh: 昭宗在華，徵拜兵部侍郎，稱足疾不任趨拜，致章謝之而已。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhaozong was at Hua, Tu was summoned and appointed vice minister of war; he claimed foot ailment and inability to perform court bows, and merely sent a memorial of thanks.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhaozong was at Hua, Tu was summoned and appointed vice minister of war. He claimed a foot ailment that prevented him from performing court bows and merely sent a memorial of thanks.

sentences.zh: 昭宗遷洛，鼎欲歸梁，柳璨希賊旨，陷害舊族，詔圖入朝。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhaozong moved to Luoyang, Ding wished to return to Liang; Liu Can curried the usurper's favor, framed the old clans, and an edict summoned Tu to court.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhaozong moved to Luoyang, Zhu Quanzhong sought to bring him under Liang control. Liu Can curried the usurper's favor, framed members of the old elite, and an edict summoned Tu to court.

sentences.zh: 圖懼見誅，力疾至洛陽，謁見之日，墮笏失儀，旨趣極野。

translations.literal: Tu feared he would be executed, forced himself through illness to reach Luoyang, and on the day of audience dropped his tablet and lost decorum; his bearing was extremely rustic.
translations.idiomatic: Tu feared execution, forced himself through illness to reach Luoyang, and on the day of audience dropped his court tablet and lost all decorum. His manner was utterly uncouth.

sentences.zh: 璨知不可屈，詔曰：「司空圖俊造登科，朱紫升籍，旣養高以傲代，類移山以釣名，心惟樂于漱流，仕非專於祿食。

translations.literal: Can knew he could not be bent and issued an edict saying: "Sikong Tu, outstanding in talent, passed the examination and rose into the purple and red registers. Having nourished loftiness to disdain the age, he is like one who moved a mountain to fish for fame. His heart delights only in rinsing in flowing streams; office is not his sole pursuit of salary and food.
translations.idiomatic: Can knew he could not be bent and issued an edict saying: "Sikong Tu, outstanding in talent, passed the examination and entered the ranks of high office. Having cultivated loftiness to disdain the age, he is like one who moved a mountain to fish for fame. His heart delights only in living as a recluse by flowing streams; office is not his sole pursuit of salary and sustenance.

sentences.zh: 匪夷匪惠，難居公正之朝；

translations.literal: Neither barbarian nor benefactor, he is hard to place in a court of impartial justice;
translations.idiomatic: Neither suitable for barbarian lands nor for a benevolent court, he is ill suited to a government of impartial justice;

sentences.zh: 載省載思，當徇棲衡之志。

translations.literal: Reflect again and again; he should follow his resolve to dwell by the gatepost.
translations.idiomatic: Upon further reflection, he should be allowed to follow his resolve to live in rustic seclusion.

sentences.zh: 可放還山。」

translations.literal: He may be released to return to the mountains."
translations.idiomatic: He is permitted to return to the mountains."

sentences.zh: 圖有先人别墅在中條山之王官谷，泉石林亭，頗稱幽棲之趣。

translations.literal: Tu had an ancestral villa in Wangguan Valley of the Zhongtiao Mountains, with springs, rocks, woods, and pavilions, quite suited to the pleasure of secluded dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: Tu had an ancestral villa in Wangguan Valley in the Zhongtiao Mountains, with springs, rocks, woods, and pavilions well suited to secluded living.

sentences.zh: 自考槃高卧，日與名僧高士遊詠其中。

translations.literal: From then on he lay high in Kaopan, daily roaming and composing poetry there with eminent monks and lofty scholars.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he lived in lofty seclusion at Kaopan, daily roaming and composing poetry there with eminent monks and reclusive scholars.

sentences.zh: 晚年為文，尤事放逹，甞擬白居易醉吟傳為休休亭記曰：司空氏禎貽溪之休休亭，本名濯纓亭，為陝軍所焚。

translations.literal: In his later years in writing he especially pursued free unrestraint; once modeling Bai Juyi's 'Biography of the Drunken Chanter' he wrote 'Record of the Rest-Rest Pavilion,' saying: The Sikong family's Rest-Rest Pavilion at Zhenyi Stream was originally named Wash-the-Tassel Pavilion and was burned by the Shan army.
translations.idiomatic: In his later writing he especially cultivated free unrestraint. Once, modeling Bai Juyi's Biography of the Drunken Chanter, he wrote Record of the Rest-Rest Pavilion: "The Sikong family's Rest-Rest Pavilion at Zhenyi Stream was originally named Wash-the-Tassel Pavilion and was burned by the Shan army."

sentences.zh: 天復癸亥歲，復葺於壞垣之中，乃更名曰休休。

translations.literal: In the guihai year of Tianfu it was rebuilt amid ruined walls, and the name was changed to Rest-Rest.
translations.idiomatic: In the guihai year of Tianfu it was rebuilt amid ruined walls, and its name was changed to Rest-Rest.

sentences.zh: 休，休也，美也，旣休而具美存焉。

translations.literal: Rest means rest, and also beauty; once rested, full beauty remains.
translations.idiomatic: Rest means repose, and also beauty; in repose, full beauty remains.

sentences.zh: 蓋量其才一宜休，揣其分二宜休，耄且聵三宜休。

translations.literal: Broadly speaking, measuring his talent, first he ought to rest; gauging his allotment, second he ought to rest; old and deaf, third he ought to rest.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly speaking: measured by talent, he ought first to rest; measured by allotted fate, he ought second to rest; old and deaf, he ought third to rest.

sentences.zh: 又少而惰，長而率，老而迂，是三者皆非濟時之用，又宜休也。

translations.literal: Moreover, idle in youth, unrestrained in maturity, and obstinate in old age—these three are none of them useful for aiding the age, and again he ought to rest.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, idle in youth, unrestrained in maturity, and obstinate in old age—these three qualities are none of them useful for aiding the age, and so again he ought to rest.

sentences.zh: 尚慮多難不能自信，旣而晝寢，遇二僧謂予曰：「吾嘗為汝師。

translations.literal: Still he worried that in many hardships he could not trust himself; then he napped by day and met two monks who said to him: "We were once your teachers.
translations.idiomatic: Still he worried that in troubled times he could not trust himself. Then he napped by day and met two monks who said to him: "We were once your teachers.

sentences.zh: 汝昔矯於道，銳而不固，為利慾之所拘，幸悟而悔，將復從我於是溪耳。

translations.literal: You once were strained in the Way, sharp yet not firm, bound by profit and desire; fortunately you awakened and repented, and will again follow us at this stream.
translations.idiomatic: You once strained after the Way, sharp yet not steadfast, bound by profit and desire. Fortunately you awakened and repented, and will again follow us at this stream.

sentences.zh: 且汝雖退，亦嘗為匪人之所嫉，宜耐辱自警，庶保其終始，與靖節、醉吟第其品級於千載之下，復何求哉！」

translations.literal: Moreover, though you have withdrawn, you have also been envied by wicked men; you should endure insult and warn yourself, so as to preserve your beginning and end, and rank your grade with Jingjie and the Drunken Chanter a thousand years hence—what more could you seek!'
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, though you have withdrawn, you have also been envied by wicked men. You should endure insult and keep yourself warned, so as to preserve your integrity from beginning to end and rank your standing with Tao Yuanming and Bai Juyi a thousand years hence. What more could you seek!"

sentences.zh: 因為耐辱居士歌，題於東北楹曰：「咄咄，休休休，莫莫莫，伎倆雖多性靈惡，賴是長教閑處著。

translations.literal: He therefore composed the Song of the Endurance-of-Insult Recluse and inscribed it on the northeast pillar, saying: "Tut-tut! Rest, rest, rest; no, no, no. Though tricks are many, nature and spirit are base; luckily one is long taught to dwell in leisure.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore composed the Song of the Endurance-of-Insult Recluse and inscribed it on the northeast pillar: "Tut-tut! Rest, rest, rest; no, no, no. Though tricks are many, nature and spirit are base; luckily one is long taught to dwell in leisure.

sentences.zh: 休休休，莫莫莫，一局棋，一爐藥，天意時情可料度。

translations.literal: Rest, rest, rest; no, no, no. One game of chess, one brazier of medicine—the intent of heaven and the mood of the age can be measured.
translations.idiomatic: Rest, rest, rest; no, no, no. One game of chess, one brazier of medicine—the intent of heaven and the mood of the age can be gauged.

sentences.zh: 白日偏催快活人，黃金難買堪騎鶴。

translations.literal: The white sun especially urges the merry man; gold cannot buy the worthiness of riding a crane.
translations.idiomatic: The white sun especially urges the merry man onward; gold cannot buy the privilege of riding a crane to immortality.

sentences.zh: 若曰：『爾何能？』

translations.literal: If one says: 'What can you do?'
translations.idiomatic: If one says: 'What can you do?'

sentences.zh: 荅云：『耐辱莫。』」

translations.literal: The answer is: 'Endure insult—nothing more.'"
translations.idiomatic: The answer is: 'Endure insult—that is all.'"

sentences.zh: 其詭激嘯傲，多此類也。

translations.literal: His eccentric vehemence, whistling, and proud disdain were mostly of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His eccentric vehemence, whistling defiance, and proud disdain were mostly of this kind.

sentences.zh: 圖既脱柳璨之禍還山，乃預為壽藏終制。

translations.literal: After Tu escaped Liu Can's peril and returned to the mountains, he beforehand prepared his tomb and final arrangements.
translations.idiomatic: After Tu escaped Liu Can's peril and returned to the mountains, he prepared his tomb and final arrangements in advance.

sentences.zh: 故人來者，引之壙中，賦詩對酌，人或難色，圖規之曰：“逹人大觀，幽顯一致，非止暫遊此中。

translations.literal: When old friends came, he led them into the burial chamber, composed poetry and drank facing them; some showed discomfort, and Tu admonished them, saying: "The man of attainment takes the great view; dark and bright are one, and this is not merely a brief visit here.
translations.idiomatic: When old friends came, he led them into the burial chamber to compose poetry and drink together. Some showed discomfort, and Tu admonished them, saying: "The man of attainment takes the great view. Dark and bright are one, and this is not merely a brief visit here.

sentences.zh: 公何不廣哉！”

translations.literal: Why do you not broaden your view!"
translations.idiomatic: Why do you not broaden your view!"

sentences.zh: 圖布衣鳩杖，出則以女家人鸞臺自隨。

translations.literal: [Close quotation.] Tu wore plain cloth and carried a dove-tailed staff; when he went out he was accompanied by the female household member Luantai.
translations.idiomatic: [Close quotation.] Tu wore plain cloth and carried a dove-tailed staff. When he went out he was accompanied by the female household member Luantai.

sentences.zh: 歲時村社雩祭祠禱，鼓舞會集，圖必造之，與野老同席，曾無傲色。

translations.literal: At seasonal village rites, rain prayers, sacrifices, and drum-and-dance gatherings, Tu always went and sat with rustic elders, never showing arrogance.
translations.idiomatic: At seasonal village rites, rain prayers, sacrifices, and drum-and-dance gatherings, Tu always attended and sat with rustic elders, never showing arrogance.

sentences.zh: 王重榮父子兄弟尤重之，伏臘饋遺，不絶於途。

translations.literal: Wang Chongrong, his sons, brothers, and father especially valued him; offerings at festivals and seasonal gifts never ceased on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chongrong and his family especially valued him. Seasonal offerings and gifts never ceased on the road to his door.

sentences.zh: 唐祚亡之明年，聞輝王遇弑于濟隂，不懌而疾，數日卒，時年七十二。

translations.literal: In the year after the Tang line perished, hearing that Prince Hui was assassinated at Jiyin, he was displeased and fell ill; within days he died, aged seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the year after the Tang dynasty fell, hearing that Prince Hui had been assassinated at Jiyin, he fell into displeasure and illness. Within days he died, at the age of seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 有文集三十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collected writings in thirty juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left collected writings in thirty juan.

sentences.zh: 圖無子，以其甥荷為嗣。

translations.literal: Tu had no son and took his nephew He as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Tu had no son and took his nephew He as his heir.

sentences.zh: 荷官至永州刺史。

translations.literal: He reached the post of prefect of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to prefect of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 以甥為嗣，甞為御史所彈，昭宗不之責。

translations.literal: Taking a nephew as heir, he was once impeached by a censor, but Emperor Zhaozong did not blame him.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had taken a nephew as heir, he was once impeached by a censor, but Emperor Zhaozong did not hold him accountable.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：國之華彩，人文化成。

translations.literal: The eulogy says: The splendor of the state, human culture formed and completed.
translations.idiomatic: The eulogy says: The splendor of the state lies in the forming and completion of human culture.

sentences.zh: 間代傑出，奮藻摛英。

translations.literal: At intervals ages produce outstanding men who stir literary ornament and unfold brilliance.
translations.idiomatic: At intervals ages produce outstanding men who stir literary ornament and unfold brilliance.

sentences.zh: 騏驥逸步，咸、韶正聲。

translations.literal: Qiji runs with swift stride; Xian and Shao are the correct sounds.
translations.idiomatic: Like swift Qiji they stride in excellence; like Xian and Shao they sound the correct music.

sentences.zh: 燦流緗素，下視姬、嬴。

translations.literal: Splendor flows through silk and plain scrolls; looking down upon Ji and Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Their brilliance flows through silk and plain scrolls, looking down even upon the ages of Ji and Ying.
